articles.body: El Atlético de Madrid recibe a Osasuna este miércoles en la búsqueda de encadenar una segunda victoria seguida antes del derbi ante el Real Madrid del próximo domingo. Los de Diego Simeone llegan de imponerse con contundencia por 3-0 en casa de la Real Sociedad, resultado que corta una racha negativa marcada por la derrota 3-0 ante el Athletic Club en San Mamés. El conjunto rojiblanco es cuarto con 10 puntos tras cinco jornadas, producto de tres victorias, un empate y una derrota. El Osasuna, por su parte, llega a Madrid tras perder 0-2 en casa ante el Espanyol, su segundo tropiezo consecutivo después de un buen arranque liguero que incluyó un empate sin goles ante el Levante y triunfos frente a Celta y Getafe. Los navarros son undécimos con siete puntos. Favorito para el partido entre Atlético de Madrid y Osasuna Con todos estos datos, las casas de apuestas dan como claro favorito al Atlético, apoyado además en un historial muy favorable como local: ha ganado 11 de sus últimos 13 duelos ante Osasuna en el Metropolitano y se impuso en las dos citas de la pasada temporada. Bet365 paga la victoria del Atlético a cuota 1.4, por 4.5 del empate y 7.5 de la victoria del cuadro rojillo. Ambos equipos marcan El mercado de ambos equipos marcan aparece como una de las alternativas más discutidas del encuentro. El Atlético ha mostrado solidez últimamente, con un 3-0 limpio en su última salida, aunque su defensa también ha encajado en las dos jornadas anteriores. El Osasuna, por su lado, ha visto puerta en cuatro de sus últimos cinco partidos de liga, pero su fragilidad como visitante —acaba de recibir dos goles del Espanyol en apenas 17 minutos— invita a pensar que el Atlético podría dejar su portería a cero. Con estos datos de las apuestas deportivas, Bet365 paga a 1.8 que al menos uno de los dos equipos se quede sin marcar, por 1.95 si ambos consiguen anotar. Número total de goles (Over/Under) El mercado de goles apunta hacia un partido con cierto potencial ofensivo, sobre todo por el dominio esperado del Atlético como local. El conjunto colchonero ha marcado en todos sus partidos de liga disputados hasta ahora, con un balance de siete goles a favor y seis en contra tras las primeras cinco jornadas. El Osasuna, aunque más discreto en ataque, ha estado involucrado en encuentros con goles en ambos lados en la mayoría de sus salidas recientes. Bet365 sitúa la cuota del +2.5 goles totales a 1.67, por 2.2 del caso contrario. Número total de córners (Over/Under) El mercado de córners se presenta como otra alternativa interesante para los apostantes. En sus últimos partidos de esta temporada, el Atlético ha promediado 5.8 saques de esquina a favor por encuentro, además de conceder una media de 5.1, lo que sitúa su promedio total de córners por partido cerca de los 10.9. El Osasuna, por el contrario, se ha movido en cifras bastante más bajas durante el curso, con 3.49 córners a favor y 3.76 en contra de media, es decir, un promedio total próximo a los 7.25 por encuentro. Con el Atlético como generador habitual de juego por bandas y un rival que suele recibir pocos córners, Bet365 paga a 1.1.91 el +9.5 córners totales, por 1.8 el caso contrario.

articles.title: England’s three-time World Cup and Premier League star Raheem Sterling could face 2 years in prison after pleading guilty
articles.summary: Football News: Former England star Raheem Sterling pleads guilty to dangerous driving, facing up to two years in prison after a motorway crash that jeopardizes his football career following a difficult spell at Feyenoord.
articles.body: Raheem Sterling is facing another uncertain chapter after appearing in court over a May motorway crash. The former England winger was convicted of dangerous driving at Basingstoke Magistrates’ Court on Tuesday, leaving him facing the possibility of a significant punishment. His football career was already at a crossroads after being released by Feyenoord following a short and underwhelming spell in the Netherlands. Now, another difficult decision awaits.Raheem Sterling has pleaded guilty to dangerous drivingSterling appeared at Basingstoke Magistrates’ Court on Tuesday, September 15, where he pleaded guilty to dangerous driving following a single-vehicle crash in May.The 31-year-old was charged last month with dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation and failing to provide a specimen.The charges relate to an incident on May 28, 2026, when Sterling was driving a Lamborghini Urus on the M25, the M3, the A327 and Minley Road before crashing into motorway barriers.Hampshire & Isle of Wight Constabulary said at the time that the collision happened on the M3 southbound near the Minley Interchange.“No other vehicles were involved, and no injuries were reported,” a force spokesperson said in a statement issued to SPORTbible.Sterling has now been convicted of dangerous driving, leaving him facing the possibility of up to two years in prison.The outcome comes at an especially difficult point in a career that once appeared destined to remain among English football's elite.Sterling's football career had already taken a sharp turnSterling's conviction arrives after several years in which his career has moved a long way from the heights he reached at Manchester City.The winger joined City from Liverpool in 2015 and became one of Pep Guardiola's most important players, winning the Premier League four times during his spell at the club.His move to Chelsea in 2022 was supposed to mark another major chapter, but his time at Stamford Bridge became increasingly difficult.Sterling made 81 appearances for Chelsea and spent part of the 2024/25 season on loan at Arsenal. By then, he was surplus to requirements in west London and was reportedly banned from using the club's facilities while in exile.His Chelsea contract was eventually terminated by mutual consent in January 2026.Sterling then signed a short-term deal with Feyenoord, where he reunited with former Manchester United and Feyenoord manager Robin van Persie. The move did not last beyond the season, however, after Sterling made just eight appearances in all competitions, playing a total of 481 minutes.Feyenoord opted not to extend his stay into the 2026/27 campaign, leaving the former England international without a club.The court case therefore arrives at a point when Sterling was already trying to work out where his football career could go next.Sterling still has options if he avoids a lengthy absenceSterling's conviction does not necessarily mean he will serve time in prison, with the maximum sentence for dangerous driving standing at two years.If he avoids a custodial sentence, his attention is likely to return to finding his next club.At 31, Sterling still has years ahead of him and remains a former 82-cap England international. He scored 20 goals and provided 19 assists for his country, representing England at three World Cups and two European Championships, including their run to the Euro 2020 final. However, his recent form and lack of regular football have made his next move difficult to predict.There was already one potential route outside England before Tuesday's court appearance.Former Liverpool, Swansea City and Newcastle midfielder Jonjo Shelvey, now manager of Dubai-based Arabian Falcons, recently revealed that the club had received enquiries from high-profile free agents.Arabian Falcons compete in the UAE Second Division League, the second tier of UAE football, and Shelvey is trying to guide them towards promotion.When asked by talkSPORT whether players including Sterling and former Manchester United winger Jadon Sancho had shown interest, Shelvey said:“There are a couple that have got in touch.“I don't really deal with that side of it. I am trying to manage the team because I want to get promoted this year.“But it is a fantastic opportunity for people if that is what they are looking for at this stage of their career, or if they are struggling to get a club.“Once the UK window shuts, you are scrambling for clubs, so we put out a call to see if there was anyone who was interested.”Dubai could offer Sterling a route back into footballSterling could now consider a move to Dubai with Arabian Falcons or wait to see whether another club in England is prepared to give him an opportunity.The UAE option would represent a significant change from the level at which Sterling spent most of his career, but it would at least give him a route back onto the pitch after his difficult spell at Feyenoord.For a player who once became a central figure in Guardiola's Manchester City side and one of England's most recognisable attackers, the immediate question is no longer where Sterling can reach his peak.It is where he goes from here.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Rodri finally reveals why he chose Barcelona over Real Madrid and what José Mourinho told him during private phone call
articles.summary: Football News: Rodri explains his decision to leave Manchester City for Barcelona, reflecting on conversations with Mourinho and his goals for success with the team.
articles.body: Rodri had plenty to think about when his next move finally came around. The decision involved two of Spain's biggest clubs, a manager he already knew well, and a conversation with José Mourinho that could easily have pulled things in another direction. Months later, the Barcelona midfielder has now explained what ultimately made up his mind.Why Rodri chose Barcelona over Real MadridThe 30-year-old's decision to leave Manchester City during the summer came as a surprise to some, particularly because Real Madrid had also pursued him. Barcelona eventually secured his signature in a reported £65.4 million move, bringing an end to seven years in England.Rodri has now explained his thinking in an interview with Spanish outlet Mundo Deportivo, making clear that the choice came down primarily to what he believed was best for his career on the pitch.“The first thing I have to say is that I would have liked it to have been a quiet two or three weeks of vacation, but it wasn't like that at all,” Rodri said.“There were many things to consider and such an important decision had to be made with two of the best clubs in the world. In the end, I made my decision based on sporting reasons, on what motivated me the most and on understanding where I could win and grow the most as a player.“It wasn't an easy decision at all; saying no to Real Madrid isn't easy, especially since they treated me exceptionally well. In the end, Deco and Hansi's leadership convinced me.”Rodri expanded on the thinking behind the move, pointing to both Barcelona's current squad and Hansi Flick's plans for the team.“I've always based my decisions on sporting merit, on where I believe I'll be able to win, be happy, and, above all, grow as a player. And that's why I chose Barça, also because of the generation of players they have and what Hansi is able to build.”The move has already begun to look encouraging. Rodri has featured five times since arriving in Catalonia, while Barcelona have made a perfect start to the season, winning all six of their opening matches across five LaLiga games and one Champions League fixture and scoring 26 goals.Barcelona have won back-to-back LaLiga titles and are now hoping Rodri's experience can help them make another step in Europe as they attempt to end an 11-year wait for the Champions League.Rodri also arrives with considerable experience of winning at the highest level. He won the 2026 FIFA World Cup with Spain in July and was awarded the Golden Ball as the tournament's best player.Rodri reveals what Mourinho said to himReal Madrid's interest was serious enough for Rodri to have a conversation with Mourinho before making his final decision.The Spain international said the Portuguese coach had “clearly expressed his desire” for him to join Madrid, although Rodri chose not to disclose the private details of their conversation.“I don't think it's appropriate to reveal a private conversation, but he clearly expressed his desire for me to come and what I could contribute to the team,” the Barcelona midfielder said.The conversation did not end badly when Rodri chose Barcelona. Instead, he said he contacted Mourinho himself to thank him for the way Madrid had handled the pursuit.“The interaction was very good. When I made my decision, I also called him to thank him for his interest and the way he treated me. I think he's a fantastic coach; I've shown him my worth wherever he's been during his successful periods, and Real Madrid is going to be a tough rival in this league.”What Rodri believes he can bring to BarcelonaRodri's role at Barcelona is not simply expected to involve controlling games from midfield. He believes his experience can also help a relatively young squad deal with situations that many of its players have yet to encounter.“I can contribute in different areas,” Rodri said. “If we're talking about experience and leadership, I think I can add a lot to a group of players that is quite young and maybe haven't faced certain situations as much as I have.“And from a footballing perspective, I am here to adapt to the team. It is already a team that works well, we have seen that they're winners already, and I want to add to that and play to my strengths.”Flick has already made clear what he expects from Rodri, with the midfielder recalling one of the first messages he received from his new manager.“One of the first things Hansi told me was about having a desire to improve day by day, to be non-conformist, to never relax, to never believe you've reached your limit and to always demand more.“That is what will lead you to success sooner or later. I believe that Barça have that room for improvement to achieve the kind of excellence that can lead to winning major European titles, having already done so in Spain.”Barcelona return to action against Racing Santander on Wednesday, September 16, with Rodri now preparing for the next stage of a decision that was ultimately made on sporting grounds rather than sentiment.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Real Madrid reportedly ready to do what they did for Ronaldo to ensure Kylian Mbappé win the 2026 Ballon d’Or
articles.summary: Football News: Real Madrid is poised to support Kylian Mbappé's 2026 Ballon d'Or aspirations, leveraging strategies from Cristiano Ronaldo's campaign. The club plans to rally legends and influence to spotlight Mbappé's achievements in a tight competition against Harry Kane and Lamine Yamal.
articles.body: Kylian Mbappé's Ballon d'Or campaign is already gathering momentum, but there is another force working behind the scenes. Real Madrid have been here before, and the club appears ready to revisit a strategy that helped Cristiano Ronaldo win the award despite strong competition from Bayern Munich.Real Madrid have a plan for Mbappé's Ballon d'Or bidMadrid are reportedly preparing to put their full institutional weight behind Mbappé in the weeks leading up to the Ballon d’Or ceremony. The club is expected to call on some of its biggest former stars and most influential figures to publicly highlight the Frenchman’s case, keeping his individual achievements at the centre of the conversation as voting draws closer.According to L’Équipe, this kind of coordinated backing has been part of Madrid’s approach in previous Ballon d’Or campaigns. The club has previously relied on respected figures from its history to champion its leading candidate, using their reputations and influence to reinforce the argument being made on the pitch.Madrid employed a similar strategy in 2013, when Alfredo Di Stéfano, Emilio Butragueño, Carlo Ancelotti, Iker Casillas and Sergio Ramos all publicly backed Cristiano Ronaldo as he competed with Bayern Munich duo Franck Ribéry and Arjen Robben.Ronaldo ultimately won the award, despite not lifting a major team trophy that year. He collected 27.99 per cent of the vote, finishing ahead of Lionel Messi on 24.72 per cent and Ribéry on 23.36 per cent.Ribéry had entered the race after helping Bayern win the Champions League, Bundesliga and German Cup, but Madrid's campaign placed greater emphasis on Ronaldo's individual achievements.Bayern's position was also complicated by the presence of Robben as another candidate from the club, meaning Ribéry did not receive the same unified backing that Ronaldo enjoyed from Madrid.The club now reportedly believes there is value in using the same approach for Mbappé.Mbappé faces Kane and Yamal in a closely fought raceThe challenge for Mbappé is that his competition is particularly strong this year.Harry Kane is currently the bookmakers' favourite, with Lamine Yamal ahead of Mbappé in some of the latest odds, leaving the Real Madrid forward in third despite an outstanding individual campaign.Kane has perhaps the strongest statistical case of the three. No player scored more club goals during the 2025-26 season, with the Bayern Munich striker finding the net 61 times as his side won both the league title and German Cup.Mbappé's case, meanwhile, rests heavily on his own production and his standing as one of the world's most influential forwards.What makes his case especially strong, despite missing out on major silverware, is his complete individual dominance across every major competition. He finished the season as the top scorer in La Liga, the Champions League, and the World Cup, racking up an astonishing 58 goals and 13 assists in 61 matches for club and country.Most notably, he captured the 2026 World Cup Golden Boot with 10 goals, a feat that simultaneously crowned him as the all-time leading scorer in World Cup history with 22 career goals.Madrid cannot manufacture a Ballon d'Or-winning season for their star, and the final decision will still come down to the journalists casting their votes. What the club can do is make sure Mbappé's achievements remain impossible to overlook during the final weeks of the campaign.How the Ballon d'Or voting worksThe Ballon d'Or is awarded annually by France Football to the player judged to have been the best in the world over a single full season.The process begins with a 30-player shortlist, created by France Football and L'Équipe. One journalist from each of the top 100 FIFA-ranked nations then votes for their top 10 players.Points are awarded according to each journalist's ranking, with voters asked to consider three principal factors.Individual performances during the previous season come first, followed by the player's team performances and achievements at both club and international level. Fair play is the third consideration, with the winner also expected to represent the sport positively as an ambassador.Once voting closes, the points are added together and the players are ranked by their totals. If two players finish level on points, the player with the greater number of first-place votes wins.Madrid hope history can repeat itselfThe club's reported strategy is therefore less about changing the voting system than about making sure its preferred candidate remains at the centre of the conversation.When former Madrid greats repeatedly argue that Mbappé deserves the award, their voices carry the weight of the club's history as well as their own reputations within football.That was the thinking behind the Ronaldo campaign in 2013, when Madrid figures collectively pushed his individual case despite the strength of Bayern's trophy haul.The circumstances are different this time, with Kane's goal-scoring record and Yamal's emergence giving voters two compelling alternatives. Yamal's strongest argument is his World Cup triumph, while domestically, he anchored Barcelona as they successfully defended their La Liga title and won the Spanish Super Cup. He was also officially named La Liga Player of the Season. Mbappé will ultimately have to make the strongest case through his performances, and the journalists will decide whether that case is enough.Madrid, however, appear unwilling to leave the result entirely to chance.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Viral TikTok video shows heartwarming other side of Iowa's iconic 'Hawkeye Wave'
articles.summary: The tradition began in September 2017, and takes place after the first quarter at every Iowa home football game.
articles.body:
TikTok user Jamie Schallock posted a side-by-side video to her account on Sunday.

On the left, it showed a view of the University of Iowa's iconic " Hawkeye Wave ," which takes place during every home game, where all the fans turn toward the children's hospital overlooking the stadium and wave. The view was from behind a window of a patient's room.

The video on the right shows Schallock and her daughter, Aria, a patient at the children's hospital.

Aria is shown taking in the view as all the fans wave. It is then explained to her that they are waving to her, and she is encouraged to wave back. The video is sure to have you blaming dust for getting in your eyes or accusing someone of cutting onions nearby.

Schallock indicated that this was the second time they had experienced the Hawkeye Wave together. The first came on Sept. 5, an experience she also captured and posted to her account .

The Hawkeye Wave began on Sept. 7, 2017. At the end of the first quarter at every home game, fans, players and coaches from both teams turn toward the University of Iowa Children's Hospital and collectively wave to the patients, letting them know they are seen and offering encouragement through whatever medical ailments they are facing.

In Aria's case, she is dealing with a Wilms tumor. It is a rare form of kidney cancer that mostly impacts children under the age of 5. Schallock has been documenting her family's experience as Aria is on the road to beating cancer.

articles.title: Ole Miss AD says he's 'tuned out' Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry, scoffs at suggestion that Lane Kiffin will need military security Saturday
articles.summary: With LSU-Ole Miss now days away, the rhetoric around Lane Kiffin's much-anticipated return to Oxford has reached ridiculous proportions.
articles.body:
With LSU-Ole Miss now days away, the rhetoric around Lane Kiffin's much-anticipated return to Oxford has reached ridiculous proportions.

Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry, who's taken an outsized role in the operations of a college football team , turned up the heat further on Monday.

Landry told ESPN's Mark Schlabach that Kiffin and his LSU team might need military security for the SEC showdown hosted by Kiffin's former Ole Miss program.

"I'm thinking about having to send him in on an F-16 and maybe the team on a C-130," Landry said. "Security is going to be really tight. You know, we might need the National Guard out there to protect our team. I think it's going to be an interesting weekend."

Schlabach noted in his report that Landry, "of course," was joking. Regardless of the tenor of Landry's comments, Ole Miss athletic director Keith Carter isn't interested in entertaining them.

Carter responded Tuesday like one might expect when another state's governor suggests that security on his campus for a football game requires the might of the U.S. military.

"Honestly, I've kind of tuned out the governor of Louisiana," Carter said in an interview with Richard Cross of 'SuperTalk Mississippi.' "That's not something that we're focused on here on campus. … We're going to make sure that we have plenty of security.

"The game's gonna go on, and everyone's gonna be just fine. We try to stay focused on the things we can control here, and, obviously, some of the rhetoric coming out of Louisiana is not something we can control."

Beyond that reasoned response, Carter declined to further take Landry's bait.

Oxford Police Chief Jeff McCutchen, meanwhile, confirmed to local media that the National Guard will not be present for Saturday's game. He did say that Oxford is enlisting the help of law enforcement from New Orleans and Mobile, Alabama, to bring in extra horse-mounted police for game day.

"I feel like it will probably be one of the biggest crowds that any of us have ever seen, and so you take that into consideration," McCutchen said, per WTVA .

Saturday's kickoff between the top-10 teams is scheduled for 7:30 p.m. ET. And one thing is for certain. The atmosphere will be electric.

articles.title: 'I need to post my Undertaker meme. We're back from the dead!' — Protect College Sports Act passes first major hurdle, but obstacles remain
articles.summary: Conference expansion was a topic that weighed heavily on the voting on Tuesday.
articles.body:
WASHINGTON — As voting concluded here at the U.S. Capitol on Tuesday, as senators sent their resounding support for a bill to regulate college athletics — the procedural first vote passed, 74-24 — the authors of the legislation, for a brief few minutes, buried their beaming happiness and postponed their celebration.

From a bird's-eye view here in the Senate gallery, one could spot Sens. Ted Cruz and Maria Cantwell, the Protect College Sports Act's leading authors, embroiled in what appeared to be an intense conversation with two of their colleagues: South Carolina Sens. Tim Scott and Darline Graham.

"You saw a little bit of scramble there," Cantwell told Yahoo Sports afterward. "We were down there really going at it."

Cantwell declined to expound on the conversation she held with the two South Carolina senators.

Surely, a similar conversation has been — or will surely be at some point — held with the senators from Florida as well.

This is all over conference expansion. A provision in the Protect College Sports Act — Section 205 — makes it more difficult for schools to move conferences. For one, it caps power conference membership at 19 schools and it requires power conference schools moving to another power league to operate as an independent for five years in a sort-of probationary period.

For all intents and purposes, the provision locks schools into their current conferences. Such schools as, say, Florida State and Miami. Or Clemson and North Carolina. Stanford too. Officials at all five school have privately voiced their resistance to a provision that, basically, prevents them from elevating to the Big Ten or SEC.

On Tuesday, at least a few of those lawmakers made noise with their votes and their voice from the Senate floor. Florida lawmakers Ashley Moody and Rick Scott were two of only four Republicans to vote against the bill (they joined Alabama's Tommy Tuberville and Kentucky's Rand Paul). And the South Carolina duo of Graham and Scott held that lengthy conversation with the bill's authors.

Whether the expansion provision changes remains an open question.

Amendments can now be filed and Cruz said he expects some of those amendments to be adopted. Cantwell left the door ajar to changes in the provision, too, but she suggested the difficulty in relaxing the provision to make it easier for, say, a host of ACC programs to leave to form what may be considered two super leagues —the SEC and Big Ten.

"People want to know that conferences are going to be strong and not undermined and that you're not going to have a ton of ways in which people are going to run off and create a super league or move around too much," she said. "But you do want to honor some flexibility."

However, what Tuesday showed is that the provision might not need to be changed to pass the legislation, at least in the Senate.

This was a blowout — 74 supportive votes (including 24 from Democrats) when only 60 were necessary to get the ball rolling. It is historic — the farthest any such, all-encompassing college sports bill has gone.

To be clear, there is plenty more time on the clock, so to speak.

(OK, we are done with the sports analogies)

You should understand that this was Vote No. 1 in a four-step voting process: three separate procedural votes, each with one full off day required between them, and then the final vote.

Sen. Eric Schmitt, a Republican from Missouri and an influential co-author on the legislation, is aiming for a final vote mid-next week. In normal legislative circumstances, a procedural vote result often reflects a future final vote, he said.

It certainly signals overwhelming support for a bill that provides the industry with what supporters say are necessary guardrails. That includes (1) re-implementing the NCAA's one-time transfer exception (limiting athletes to one transfer before having to miss a season of eligibility); (2) establishing a five-year eligibility standard (and banning pro players — a recent hot topic); (3) increasing the per-school annual athlete revenue-share payments to around $48 million, up from $21 million, and provides the NCAA and College Sports Commission with legal protections to enforce such; and (4) creating an agent registry and certification system capping agent commission at 5%.

Those are the bill's primary components. It does plenty of other things, like preventing coaches from leaving mid-season (dubbed the Lane Kiffin Rule) and permits FBS conferences to consolidate their media rights like the NFL (though that's unlikely — just ask the SEC and Big Ten).

The landslide vote Tuesday means the legislation that so many doubted has a real chance in the next chamber, the House of Representatives. Leadership in the House has expressed skepticism over the bill and they decided earlier this month to break for recess after this week and not return until mid-November.

"When the Senate passes the bill [in the final vote], I believe the House will take it up and pass it," he told Yahoo Sports from the Capitol. "I fully expect this will be signed into law before Election Day."

Midterm elections are Nov. 3. Will the House decide to return to session to take up the college sports bill before then? President Donald Trump, an ardent supporter of the bill, has held communication with House leadership about the prospect, those with knowledge of the talks tell Yahoo Sports.

"It's not out of the realm of possibility for them to take it up," Schmitt said. "I think there is a strong desire to not let this lapse and go past the midterms."

In fact, during a robust speech on the Senate floor before the procedural vote, Sen. Cory Booker, a former Stanford football player, eviscerated the legislation, calling it an "unjust bill" that doesn't protect athletes enough and grants sweeping antitrust powers to a monopolized entity (the NCAA).

Those opposing the legislation often point to the fact that the bill restricts athlete movement and establishes a harder cap on their pay without touching the millions going to administrators and coaches. Many of them would prefer the conferences and schools bargain directly with the athletes — something that, while rife with obstacles and legal hurdles, they believe is a more fair course of action.

As it turns out, that pushback seemed to bury the bill last month, when senators got to the doorstep of a vote before opposition mounted.

"I need to post my Undertaker meme. We're back from the dead!" Schmitt said outside of the Senate chambers.

But for some, all of the issues aren't fixed. The conference expansion provision lingers as problematic, not just in the Senate but in the House too.

"Republican senators who would normally be inclined to support this bill are now withholding support due to the provision basically locking schools into conferences for eternity," said one Senate staff member. "It could possibly tank the bill."

At least through one round, it did not. Suffice to say, the clock hasn't hit zeros yet.

articles.title: Chess Olympiad: Uzbeks face tough test from defending champs India
articles.summary: Chess News: Former champions Uzbekistan will be severely tested as their men will try to regain the Olympiad chess title that they won in India four years ago.Uzb.
articles.body: Former champions Uzbekistan will be severely tested as their men will try to regain the Olympiad chess title that they won in India four years ago.Uzbekistan will feel the added pressure of home expectations at Samarkand coupled with the might of defending champions India in the 11-round over-the-board classical tournament. They had stopped India's winning spree with draws in 2022 and 2024 editions of the biennial team event. Their then captain Vladimir Kramnik had dubbed the match two years ago in Budapest as "real chess" (all-drawn games with no blunders) when other teams crumbled against marauding individual gold medallists D Gukesh on the top board and Erigaisi Arjun on the third.Most importantly, the 46th Olympiad - with record 399 teams across two sections - also provides Gukesh a chance to regain his form in the team atmosphere with the motivation of playing for the tricolour before his title defence against Sindarov in Geneva that starts on Nov 24. In the last two Olympiads, he was the player of the tournament before winning the world crown at age 18 in late 2024 that seems to be weighing heavy on his shoulders.Now captained by V Anand's former second Rustam Kasimdzhanov, Uzbeks have the new chess star Javokhir Sindarov as their top rated player, a world No. 4 at 2778. "It was unimaginable that we would host an event of this magnitude six-seven years ago," said Nodirbek Abdusarttorov (age 21) at a press conference on Tuesday. "But thanks to the support and hard work of players, it is made possible."India had won the double gold in both sections last time. They too have high expectations to deal with. The women's team, comprising K Humpy, World Cup winner Divya Deshmukh and world championship challenger R Vaishali are the top seeds because Russia remains banned from team competitions and China have not sent their full-strength team. And despite having the most exciting trinity - of world champion D Gukesh, in-form R Praggnanandhaa and Arjun - in their ranks, the Indian men are not the top seeds in the open event. articles.title: Candidato al ascenso, pero colista en límite salarial
articles.standfirst: El Almería tiene el Límite de Coste de Plantilla Deportiva más bajo de Primera y Segunda, pero eso no significa que tengan el presupuesto más reducido ni una plantilla barata
articles.summary: El Almería tiene el Límite de Coste de Plantilla Deportiva más bajo de Primera y Segunda, pero eso no significa que tengan el presupuesto más reducido ni una plantilla barata
articles.body: Los nuevos Límites de Coste de Plantilla Deportiva (LCPD), publicados por LaLiga hace unos días, han vuelto a generar sorpresa. El Almería aparece con el menor límite de todos los equipos de Primera y Segunda división, fijado en apenas 3,975 millones de euros. Sin embargo, la realidad deportiva dice todo lo contrario: los rojiblancos cuentan con una de las plantillas más potentes de LaLiga Hypermotion y, según el valor de mercado de Transfermarkt, sólo el Girona presenta un plantel más valioso entre los 22 clubes de la categoría de plata. La pregunta es inevitable: ¿cómo puede suceder? La respuesta está en que el conocido popularmente como límite salarial no es, en realidad, un límite de salarios. El LCPD incluye sueldos, primas, Seguridad Social, amortizaciones de fichajes, comisiones, cuerpo técnico e incluso determinados gastos del filial. Tampoco representa el presupuesto del club ni el coste real de la plantilla. En el caso del Almería, la explicación hay que buscarla en el descenso desde Primera división. Durante su etapa en la máxima categoría, el club firmó contratos largos y asumió costes propios de una plantilla diseñada para competir en la élite. Al bajar, los ingresos se redujeron drásticamente, pero los contratos ya firmados siguieron vigentes. Los futbolistas continúan teniendo contrato y el club debe asumir esos compromisos económicos. Por eso, el coste real de la plantilla puede ser muy superior al LCPD fijado por LaLiga. No existe ninguna obligación de reducir automáticamente el gasto cuando baja el límite, ya que los contratos deben respetarse. La diferencia aparece a la hora de inscribir nuevos jugadores. Ahí es donde el Almería se ha visto obligado durante los últimos mercados a generar margen económico mediante ventas importantes, liberación de salarios y la búsqueda de incorporaciones con un coste reducido, ya sea a través de cesiones, futbolistas libres u operaciones con una inversión muy controlada. El objetivo no es otro que ir acercando progresivamente el coste de la plantilla al límite que considera sostenible LaLiga. Otro aspecto que suele generar confusión son los fichajes. Que un club pague varios millones por un jugador no significa que esa cantidad consuma íntegramente el límite de esa temporada. El traspaso se amortiza durante los años de contrato. Es decir, un futbolista fichado por 15 millones y firmado por cinco temporadas computa tres millones por curso en concepto de amortización, a los que habría que añadir su salario y el resto de costes asociados. Por todo ello, el dato de los 3,975 millones no significa que la plantilla del Almería cueste menos de cuatro millones ni que sea una de las más baratas de Segunda. Lo que refleja es la situación económica que debe alcanzar el club según el sistema de control financiero de LaLiga. El club está fuera de la norma 1:1 para poder inscribir con normalidad, aunque tiene un pequeño margen para poder firmar en enero si así lo decidiera. Mientras tanto, la entidad continúa gestionando una plantilla heredada de su etapa en Primera, una circunstancia que explica por qué el equipo puede seguir siendo uno de los grandes candidatos al ascenso pese a aparecer el último en la tabla del Límite de Coste de Plantilla Deportiva.

articles.title: La detención de Sterling por conducción temeraria mientras se drogaba con gas de la risa: "No se tense"
articles.standfirst: Se han publicado las imágenes de la cámara corporal de la policía durante la detención del futbolista Raheem Sterling por conducción temeraria mientras se drogada con hippy crack
articles.summary: Se han publicado las imágenes de la cámara corporal de la policía durante la detención del futbolista Raheem Sterling por conducción temeraria mientras se drogada con hippy crack
articles.body: Raheem Sterling, futbolista 82 veces internacional con Inglaterra que jugó en Arsenal, Chelsea, Liverpool y Manchester City, sufrió un accidente en su Lamborghini Urus (315.000 euros) y fue detenido por la Policía cerca del enlace de Minley en la autopista M3 (Hampshire). Una conductora declaró a la Policía que, al mirar hacia el otro vehículo, vio al conductor del Lamborghini con un globo (inflado con la droga hippy crack) frente a la cara; este era tan grande que ella llegó a pensar que se trataba de un airbag. "Era temprano por la mañana y vi el Lamborghini en la autopista mientras iba al trabajo, así que miré rápidamente por curiosidad quién lo conducía. Reconocí a Sterling de inmediato y luego vi que llevaba un globo en las manos; no podía creerlo, supe al instante que debía de ser gas de la risa. Me pareció una conducta totalmente temeraria mientras conducía... Podría haber sufrido un accidente con él aquel día y mis hijos se habrían quedado sin madre; su comportamiento es totalmente inaceptable", explicó la conductora al diario 'The Sun'. El delantero de 31 años, que la pasada temporada jugó en el Feyenoord, confesó tener un problema con el consumo de óxido nitroso (el popular hippy crack o gas de la risa, cuyo consumo está penado en Inglaterra desde 2023). Sterling se ha declarado culpable del cargo de conducción peligrosa, del de posesión de drogas y de uno adicional por no haber podido dar una muestra de su aliento. Durante la vista en el Tribunal de Magistrados de Basingstoke, se expuso que Sterling presentaba tal grado de afectación por el gas de la risa que era incapaz de realizar pruebas básicas en comisaría, como tocarse la nariz con el dedo o caminar colocando un pie delante del otro. "Sterling parecía callado, retraído y aletargado, además de mostrarse inquieto y moverse constantemente. Tenía los párpados caídos, un signo compatible con la fatiga o la intoxicación por drogas. Afirmaba sentir mucho frío, a pesar de que nos encontrábamos en plena ola de calor, con temperaturas de 33 grados", describió el abogado Simon Jones. El 'Daily Mail' publica que las imágenes de la cámara corporal de la policía muestran el momento en que Sterling fue detenido con seis cartuchos de óxido nitroso y un globo desinflado en el regazo. Se escucha a un agente decirle al futbolista "puedes dejar eso ahí" tras abrir la puerta del coche. A continuación, se le ve retirar los objetos de su regazo y colocarlos detrás del asiento. Le preguntan a Sterling "¿puedes salir un momento?" y quién conducía en el momento del accidente, pero no responde. El agente de policía añade: "Así que se niega a responder, de acuerdo". Se le ordena a Sterling que salga del vehículo; al borde de la carretera le preguntan su nombre y edad, y le dicen: "Deje el teléfono, déjese de juegos. No se tense". A continuación, se le leen sus derechos y se procede a su detención, tras pedirle que coloque los brazos a la espalda.

articles.title: Contra el poder inglés
articles.standfirst: El músculo financiero de la clase media de la Premier se hace notar en una Europa League que ha tenido cuatro campeones en la última década y dos (Tottenham y Aston Villa) de forma consecutiva
articles.summary: El músculo financiero de la clase media de la Premier se hace notar en una Europa League que ha tenido cuatro campeones en la última década y dos (Tottenham y Aston Villa) de forma consecutiva
articles.body: La Europa League está empezando a convertirse en una especie de 'coto privado' para la Premier. El músculo financiero del que presume su clase media viene marcando unas diferencias respecto al resto de ligas del Viejo Continente que se antoja insalvable. En la última década, ha habido cuatro campeones provenientes de la competición inglesa... mientras que Tottenham y Aston Villa se han alzado con las dos últimas ediciones. Esta temporada, además, contarán con tres representantes. Por la 'vía Premier', Bournemouth y un recién ascendido Sunderland dieron la 'campanada' logrando la clasificación por delante de tres equipos que venían de competir en Champions como Chelsea, Newcastle y el propio Tottenham. A ellos, se suma un Crystal Palace que logró su billete gracias al triunfo en la final de la Conference League contra el Rayo Vallecano. No son, eso sí, los equipos ingleses con más 'pedigrí' que han pasado por la competición en los últimos años y, desde luego, van a tener competencia en busca de enlazar su tercer título consecutivo en esta Europa League. Hay, de hecho, hasta seis equipos que participaron en la pasada Champions. Desde España, sin ir más lejos, regresa la Real Sociedad como campeón de la Copa del Rey —mismo caso que el AZ en Países Bajos— y repite un Celta que quiere hacer valer la experiencia adquirida durante la temporada pasada. De Alemania, además del Hoffenheim, regresa un Bayer Leverkusen que se quedó a las puertas de alzar el trofeo en 2024 de la mano de Xabi Alonso. Ahora bien, si nos referimos a campeones de la máxima competición continental, esta edición cuenta con varios equipos que cuentan con alguna 'Orejona' en sus vitrinas. Desde Italia, sin ir más lejos, se presentan Milan y Juventus. Dos conjuntos que, por historia, no deberían estar aquí... pero su momento presente así lo definió en la última jornada de la Serie A con un desenlace dramático para ambos. A ellos, además, también se adhiere un Olympique de Marsella que, hasta que el PSG implantó su dinastía, podía presumir de ser el único conjunto francés que había levantado la Champions. Han atravesado, eso sí, un verano en el que se han visto obligados a desprenderse de sus mejores jugadores. Se les une el Rennes y su prolífica academia. Desde las rondas previas apareció un 'coco' como Benfica. Y es que, a pesar de finalizar invictos la Primeira Liga de la mano de Mourinho, acabaron cayendo a la Europa League. El principal responsable fue un Torreense que, como campeón de Taça, se ganó el derecho a participar en esta edición... ¡militando en Segunda división! Una edición más, la Europa League parte con una infinidad de aspirantes para hacerse con el título que se decidirá el próximo 26 de mayo de 2027 sobre el tapete del Deutsche Bank Park de Frankfurt. Como curiosidad, ninguno de los campeones desde el cambio de formato (2009) participará en la presente edición. Esta primera jornada de la Europa League 26-27, de forma excepcional, se repartirá entre miércoles y jueves. El gran plato fuerte, sin lugar a dudas, será el duelo que acoge San Siro entre Milan y Benfica. Será un partido especial para Rúben Amorim, quien colgó las botas en Da Luz en 2017... aunque posteriormente se hizo un nombre en los banquillos a los mandos del Sporting CP. Tiene claro, eso sí, que están aquí "para ganar el torneo". No será menos para Gonçalo Ramos, fichaje más caro en la historia del Milan... que en su momento dejó 65 millones en las arcas de Benfica cuando fichó por el PSG en 2023 tras conquistar el último título de Liga de las 'águilas'. "Es mi casa; he pasado más tiempo allí que con mi familia. Claro que quiero marcar, pero no lo celebraría", admitió. También habrá muchas miradas puestas en el duelo que enfrenta al Jagiellonia de Jesús Imaz ante un Olympiacos donde ya no está José Luis Mendilibar. Su puesto en el banquillo de El Pireo fue ocupado por un Imanol Alguacil que se estrenó con derrota en casa ante el OFI. Querrá, por tanto, darle su primera alegría a una afición siempre exigente.

articles.title: Jan Virgili, un 'diablo' entre Brujas: "Puede convertirse en un extremo de primer nivel en Europa"
articles.standfirst: El ex de Mallorca y Barcelona ya sabe lo que es marcar y asistir en el Jan Breydel Stadium
articles.summary: El ex de Mallorca y Barcelona ya sabe lo que es marcar y asistir en el Jan Breydel Stadium
articles.body: Apenas seis partidos (259') le han bastado a Jan Virgili (Vilasar de Mar, 2006) para 'meterse en el bolsillo' al Jan Breydel Stadium. Al ex de Barcelona y Mallorca, fichado a cambio de 12 millones de euros, no parece pesarle el hecho de ser el segundo fichaje más caro en la historia del Brujas. Sólo por Roman Yaremchuk (17) pagaron más. El español, nominado al 'Golden Boy', está llamado a perpetuar la larga lista de extremos que los 'blauw-zwart' han exportado a las grandes Ligas en los últimos años: Tzolis, Nusa, Skov Olsen, Diatta... En su debut en Champions -coincidía con su estreno como titular- 'regaló' una asistencia a Hugo Vetlesen a los 19 minutos de juego. No sirvió, sin embargo, para evitar la derrota ante el Aston Villa (2-3). Se redimió a lo grande, jugando también de inicio, en la victoria sobre el Amberes (3-1). El internacional sub 21 provocó el penalti con el que Vetlesen 'abrió la lata' en el 13' y rubricó el triunfo anotando el definitivo 3-1 en el 78'. Recibió en largo de Joaquin Seys, recortó a Somers, Tsunashima y Mauricio Benítez y volvió sobre sus pasos para fusilar a Nozawa con un potente zurdazo al palo corto. Puso la guinda celebrándolo con un mortal mientras sus padres, su hermano Nill y su agente, Nacho Monreal, aplaudían desde la grada. "Es posiblemente el gol más bonito que he marcado en mi vida. Estoy muy contento con mi partido. El premio al 'Mejor Jugador' del partido está muy bien, pero lo que importa es el equipo. Soy muy feliz aquí en Brujas. Me siento bien. Venir aquí fue la decisión correcta", reconocía Virgili en los micrófonos de 'DAZN'. Su 'MVP' generó unanimidad. "Fue el mejor jugador sobre el terreno de juego. Estuvo realmente bien. Es un fichaje millonario que está demostrando que tiene que sitio equipo. Provocó un penalti, marcó un buen gol...", advirtió el exfutbolista Gert Verheyen en 'Zondag Matchdag'. Su compañero Joaquin Seys también se deshizo en elogios hacia Virgili: "Fue uno de los más destacados contra el Amberes, pero ya venía de jugar un gran partido contra el Aston Villa. El otro día dio una asistencia. Es genial que ahora también haya marcado su primer gol. Es un jugador excelente: entiende muy bien el juego, tiene mucha potencia y sabe desmarcarse". Ferran Jutglá, ex del Brujas, intercedió para que Jan Virgili acabara en el Jan Breydel Stadium y a otro español le tocó sufrirle. "Somos buenos amigos. Marcó un golazo. Le deseo lo mejor; puede convertirse en un extremo de primer nivel en Europa", señaló el exazulgrana Álvaro Cortés, ahora en el Amberes. Un 'diablo' anda suelto por Brujas.

articles.standfirst: Jonathan David se estrena en un Metropolitano... que ya conquistó con un doblete hace dos campañas vistiendo la camiseta del Lille
articles.summary: Jonathan David se estrena en un Metropolitano... que ya conquistó con un doblete hace dos campañas vistiendo la camiseta del Lille
articles.body: Ni su afición asistió a su estreno como goleador del Atlético ni ha precisado vestir la camiseta rojiblanca para conquistar el Metropolitano, pero la realidad es que Jonathan David se bautiza como futbolista local precedido por su goles. De ahí que en la que será su primera vez en la nueva casa el canadiense llega avalado por sus tarjetas de presentación. Con Sorloth aún en la enfermería y con Julián Alvarez sometido a los máximos cuidados para que pueda recuperarse a tiempo para el derbi del domingo, Jonathan David aprovecha su momento para reivindicar su candidatura al 9. Media hora le bastó en Anoeta, prácticamente el mismo tiempo que le llevó silenciar al Metropolitano el 23 de octubre de 2024. Argumentos de peso ambos para optar a ser el elegido como punta de lanza ante Osasuna. Aunque Grimaldo ya había inclinado el duelo hacia el Atlético, el gol firmado por Jonathan David a la Real, tras dejar a varios defensas por el camino a golpe de cadera, le catapulta a cobrar protagonismo ante el cuadro rojillo. De hecho, antes de dibujar su golazo ya había exigido una gran respuesta de Remiro tras sacarse un disparo al palo largo con el que culminaría sus amagos previos. Un delantero que recordó al que apuntilló al Atlético en la Champions justo después de que Sorloth completara una noche repleta de fallos ante el marco rival. De nada valdría el gol de Julián, pues la entrada en escena de Jonathan David para marcar de penalti, primero, y en el área, después, le erigiría en el héroe de aquel 1-3.

articles.title: Turno para el Metropolitano
articles.standfirst: El Atlético regresa a casa tras cuatro partidos seguidos como visitante. Osasuna y Real Madrid, los rivales
articles.summary: El Atlético regresa a casa tras cuatro partidos seguidos como visitante. Osasuna y Real Madrid, los rivales
articles.body: Sevilla, Bilbao, Liverpool y San Sebastián. Cuatro paradas lejos del Metropolitano para los de Simeone. Dos triunfos y dos derrotas. Ahora toca volver a casa tras un último partido como locales de lo más accidentado. La última vez que los rojiblancos jugaron un encuentro en su casa el mercado seguía abierto y el caso Julián condicionó todo. Un empate ante el Villarreal en medio de una tormenta de pitos. Mal recuerdo que ahora toca cambiar en una semana en la que los del Cholo jugarán dos encuentros como anfitriones. Osasuna, el miércoles, y el derbi ante el Madrid, el domingo. Dos duelos antes de marcharse al parón de selecciones para irse con las mejores sensaciones posibles. Dos victorias dejarían a los rojiblancos en una situación casi inmejorable tras un comienzo de curso de los más cuesta arriba posible con cuatro salidas consecutivas. Las tres ligueras se solventaron con seis puntos de nueve posibles. El borrón de San Mamés duele menos tras la contundente victoria ante la Real Sociedad. La segunda parte del duelo ante el Athletic es el espejo en el que mirarse para que no vuelve a suceder como visitantes. Pero ahora toca jugar de locales. Algo que durante las últimas temporadas se ha convertido en una de las grandes fortalezas del Atlético del Cholo. Temporada tras temporadas el Metropolitano se ha convertido en uno de los grandes fortines de LaLiga. Los de Simeone han firmado una media de 45 puntos como locales desde que se mudaron a su nueva casa en 2017. Desde entonces, en ningún curso bajaron de los 41 puntos como locales siendo en la 23/24 donde lograron su mayor puntuación con 49 puntos. El Metropolitano es una de las grandes fortalezas rojiblancas y el propio Simeone tiene claro que necesitan a su gente. Con la más que previsible baja de Julián para el duelo ante Osasuna, el argentino intentará estar disponible para el derbi del domingo, el Atlético espera que el Metropolitano recupere la calma. El choque ante el Villarreal estuvo marcado por un ambiente muy negativo que pudo afectar al equipo. Tras el penalti y la expulsión de Le Normand, el estadio llevó en volandas al equipo para buscar el empate que finalmente llegó con una gran acción de Giuliano tras pase de Baena. Un punto que supo a oro tras lo vivido esa tarde. Ahora, sin la presencia del argentino, se espera de nuevo recuperar la fortaleza en el Metropolitano.

articles.body: KOLKATA: East Bengal FC look to keep the early-season momentum going as Antonio Lopez Habas’s team begins its AFC Champions League Two campaign against reigning Jordanian champions Al Hussein in Amman on Wednesday.Last month, East Bengal qualified for the revamped second tier of Asian club football by brushing aside Kuwait’s Al Arabi SC and followed it with their Durand Cup triumph with another dominating performance against arch-rivals Mohun Bagan SG.“We are excited to participate in the ACL Two group stage. We want to continue the winning momentum that we’ve achieved over the past two months. We want to replicate that success in the game against Al-Hussein,” Habas said during a press conference in Amman on Tuesday.The reigning Indian champions landed in Jordan with only three foreigners — Dani Ramirez, Mohammed Rashid and Croatian newcomer Diego Zivulic, but Habas kept his faith in the domestic firepower. David Lalhlansanga and Edmund Lalrindika’s performances against Al Arabi and Mohun Bagan have proved that they are capable of carrying the team’s ambitions on big occasions.“I think East Bengal now have (got) the level of playing (in away matches). Never do I play for a draw and the idea is always to win the match. Because the moment you stop thinking about the possibility of winning, it will finish your career as a coach,” Habas said before leaving for Jordan.Al Hussein are hosting East Bengal at a time when the home team’s house seems to be in disorder. articles.title: Craig Bellamy: Does Wales head coach need to win back fans?
articles.summary: After a "sleepless night", Wales boss Craig Bellamy decided to turn down the chance to manage Burnley - but has it affected what fans think of him?
articles.body:
Cristiano Ronaldo in Lisbon, Erling Haaland at home and a double-header with a Denmark side they have not beaten in 18 years as Wales return to Nations League A.

But does head coach Craig Bellamy face his own challenge?

Supporters were already smarting from missing out on the World Cup. Then their mood darkened further as it emerged Bellamy had held talks over becoming boss at Burnley.

The 47-year-old admitted to a "sleepless night" when coming to a decision to either stay with Wales or succeed Scott Parker at Turf Moor, the club he had previously served as an assistant boss under Vincent Kompany.

Bellamy said he went with his gut to turn down Burnley and that he had unfinished business with his national side.

Nevertheless, some pundits have suggested the 78-cap former striker now needs to win back support after such speculation over his future.

Bellamy suggested he did not know whether that is the situation he faces over the next three weeks - and beyond - after reiterating his ambition to lead Wales to a home Euro 2028.

Even so, given that as a player Bellamy once had a legal tussle with his club in order to be available for his country, is it fair to question his commitment?

Bellamy 'committed' to Wales after Burnley talks

Rodon absent as Ashford earns first Wales call-up

'I've proven my commitment over the years' - what Bellamy says

Bellamy says he has a "gift" of not taking what people say to heart, but he will have heard queries over his commitment before.

"I think with my body of work over the years, I don't think I need to say too much about that," he said, after announcing his squad for the first four games of the new Nations League campaign – the first international matches since the Burnley saga.

"I think my commitment has always been there and I've proven that over the years.

"I remember I had to go and get solicitors' letters from independent people because my club at the time were trying to tell me not to play [for Wales] and they would sue me if I did. I haven't seen anyone else do that."

There are other examples of Bellamy's commitment to Welsh football.

He donated money to Wrexham when they were in financial difficulty during his playing days, while there have been claims that he has not claimed expenses from the Football Association of Wales (FAW) either as a Wales player or coach.

"Wales is way more important to me," he said. "I don't believe I have to ever try to win anyone over with that."

But has the Burnley episode changed that?

Bellamy has denied that his decision not to join the club side was based on an issue with backroom staff. He says that instead it came down to what he felt was right, and that he left a lucrative offer on the table.

He suspected that Burnley had expected him to take the job and felt there was surprise and disappointment when he said no.

"I had a sleepless night because I knew it had become real," added Bellamy.

"I have to be honest, I woke up in the morning and it wasn't there. I didn't have that feeling of going into a meeting and grabbing it.

"You don't know until that moment comes, but to me, it has to mean the most to me."

But is that enough for some? Or - as Bellamy himself has suggested - will it take a return to winning ways and putting World Cup disappointment to bed to fully draw a line under things?

'A few wins and flirtations will be a distant memory' - a fan's verdict

Ryan March, Wales regular and editor of fanzine Alternative Wales :

"We obviously don't know what goes on behind closed doors - and if what is being reported is gospel, or what Bellamy himself says is fact.

"So, it all depends on what or who you believe, but the fact is Craig Bellamy now has even more work to do to get the fans back on side.

"We all saw that Bosnia-Herzegovina game as a huge missed opportunity [to reach a World Cup finals] and, for most of us, the blame lies at Craig Bellamy's door for his game management.

"The summer's friendlies only added to that frustration as we lacked any sort of performance - and most fans were OK with the idea of him going to Burnley.

"The only way Bellamy can truly win the fans back ahead of next year's Euro 2028 campaign is by winning games and [producing] good performances. That's the simple fact.

"If we go and win a few of these Nations League games and stay in Group A, the flirtations with Burnley will be a distant memory."

'His commitment won't change' - a pundit's verdict

Rob Earnshaw, former Wales striker and Match of the Day Wales pundit :

"I'm glad that he's still here because I think he moves Wales forward if he's in charge.

"There's always going to be Wales fans that are looking for the manager to impress them, looking for the manager to do more.

"The only thing that I know he can control is if he wins games - and things will be better. So that's the aim, but that's going to be difficult with some big games coming up.

"The only other thing that I can speak for, knowing and understanding Craig, is that his commitment won't change with Wales.

"If we were talking about two clubs, maybe that would be different. But with Wales, the commitment doesn't change.

"His drive to make the team better, make players better, trying to win us games, is going be the same - and that's going to be relentless.'

articles.title: La 'nueva' Serie A hace historia: 40 partidos y ningún 0-0, 3.9 goles de media por partido...
articles.standfirst: La 2026-27 en Italia ha comenzado como nunca antes
articles.summary: La 2026-27 en Italia ha comenzado como nunca antes
articles.body: Por primera vez en la historia del fútbol italiano, tras las cuatro primeras jornadas de una temporada no se ha registrado ningún 0-0 en Serie A o Serie B. O lo que es lo mismo, 80 partidos entre Primera y Segunda División en Italia... y siempre ha habido al menos un gol. En el caso de la élite del 'Calcio', la última fecha, disputada este pasado fin de semana, registró un total de 39 tantos. Es decir, 3.9 goles por partido. Casi nada. Este artículo, sin embargo, no es una oda al 'renacer' del fútbol italiano. Ni mucho menos. La selección 'Azzurra' sigue sin levantar cabeza acumulando tres Mundiales ausente y los equipos de la Serie A no son favoritos a ganar la Champions... sobre todo porque no tienen el dinero para poder justificar su candidatura. Pero hay brotes verdes, eso seguro. Un 'despertar' que ha coincidido con las nuevas directrices de Daniele Orsato. El ex colegiado fue elegido jefe arbitral tras el escándalo de Gianluca Rocchi... y su decisión de 'europeizar' el 'Calcio' ha sido todo un éxito. En realidad, no ha hecho nada nuevo salvo implementar la nueva reglamentación de la International Football Association Board (que ya vimos en el Mundial) en la Serie A. Es decir, reducir las pérdidas de tiempo al máximo y buscar un ritmo de juego mucho más alto. Y ha funcionado: el tiempo efectivo registrado en los partidos de Serie A es el más alto registrado desde que se mide dicho parámetro. La cuenta atrás del colegiado en los saques de portería y saques de banda, el tiempo límite para realizar un cambio... o, incluso, el mero hecho de dejar jugar salvo faltas flagrantes. Un dato resume esto: solamente se han pitado dos penaltis en 40 partidos de Serie A 2026-27. Y si bien es cierto que en algunos casos ha habido errores de VAR que han dejado penas máximas sin señalar, ha quedado patente que un contacto dentro del área ya no siempre es sancionable. El mejor ejemplo es el Monza. El equipo de Ivan Juric lleva un punto de 12 posibles pero es el sexto equipo de Italia que más goles esperados produce: casi dos por partido. En su caso, la defensa y le portero los lastra al fondo de la tabla. Pero equipos como el Como (Fàbregas), la Roma (Gasperini), Sassuolo (Aquilani), Inter (Chivu), Milan (Amorim) o Frosinone (Alvini) son proyectos con ideas ofensivas y de protagonismo claramente predominantes. Ante Udinese, el Inter ganó 5-3 (en un partido que empezó 0-2) y acumuló 27 disparos contra el arco rival; ante Atalanta, la Roma remontó un 0-1 tras disparar en 39 ocasiones. Incluso la Fiorentina, que despidió a Fabio Grasso tras tres jornadas y cero puntos sumados, va al ataque: 7.46 goles esperados en cuatro jornadas; o lo que es lo mismo, el tercer mejor equipo de Italia en esa métrica. El nivel defensivo, sin embargo, ha caído. Poco queda de aquellas defensa inexpugnables que lideraban todos y cada uno de los equipos italianos. Pero no habría cambios sin jóvenes talentos... e Italia ha pasado de ser una liga con una durísima crítica interna por no apostar por su cantera a marcar los mejores registros en mucho tiempo. De los 119 goles anotados este curso por los 20 equipos del 'Calcio', 49 los firman jugadores de 23 años o menos. La Serie A es la segunda gran liga con mayores Sub23 partiendo de inicio como titulares en esta 2026-27... y en la que menos jugadores mayores de 33 años se alinean. Equipos como el Parma (23,4 años de edad media), el Monza (23,5), Frosinone (23,7), Fiorentina (24,2), Como (24,5), Sassuolo (24,7) o Cagliari (25) tienen números propios de ligas que son 'viveros' como la Eredivisie de Países Bajos o la Pro League belga. Aunque venga de fuera. El Como ha invertido casi 400 millones de euros desde que la familia Hartono (Indonesia) lo compró en Serie C siendo el ejemplo más claro de renovación y éxito en un tiempo récord. Y sin embargo, una inversión cuidadosamente medida. Esa cantidad, 400 'kilos', los ha gastado el Manchester City solamente en este pasado mercado de verano. Los lombardos han invertido bien en Baturina (18 millones), Milla (6), Diao (12), Perrone (13), Jacobo (2,5) o Álex Valle (6), por mencionar algunos nombres. Este mercado recién terminado, por ejemplo, evidenció dos cosas: que la Premier se mantiene como la liga que más gasta del mundo (con una diferencia salvaje sobre el resto, 4.080 millones de euros)... pero también que la Serie A es la segunda. El 'Calcio' invirtió 1.160 millones de euros por los 782 de la Bundesliga, los 755 de LaLiga o los 605 de la Ligue 1 francesa. Una situación que se explica, en parte, por la gran cantidad de propietarios extranjeros que inyectan dinero en el fútbol italiano: Un aspecto que, sin embargo, hay que coger con pinzas pues clubes como el Inter o el Milan están 'capados' por políticas de fichajes de gasto muy reducido... buscando la viabilidad de la entidad y la constante rebaja de la masa salarial. Pero el potencial está ahí... sobre todo porque Italia ha sido un gigante dormido durante demasiado tiempo. Un aspecto que ya definió a la perfección alguien 'nuevo' como Suwarso, el Presidente del Como: "¿Qué tiene la Premier que no tengamos nosotros en Italia? Dinero. Pero nosotros tenemos historia, arte, gastronomía y pasión".

articles.title: Why are Man Utd better without the ball?
articles.summary: Under Michael Carrick, Manchester United average 1.5 points per game when they have more than 50% of the ball. When they have less than 50%, this number is 2.6.
articles.body:
Under Michael Carrick, Manchester United average only 1.5 points per game when they have more than 50% of the ball. When they have less than 50%, this number shoots up to 2.6.

And if you drop possession further, to 45% or below, United have won 10 games out of the past 10 since Carrick took the job.

It is a staggering correlation but it brings the Englishman to the same crossroads that former United manager Ole Gunnar Solskjaer found himself at.

How do you bridge the game from a seemingly elite counter-attacking side to one capable of beating teams that give you the ball?

Going down to 10 men on the way to a 1-0 derby defeat is far from ideal, but at full-time Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca offered a different perspective.

"We had a plan for 11 versus 11, but after the red card the game completely changed, but also for them.

"They love transitions and space in behind, but the game became more difficult.

"We just dropped, [offering] no space in behind and no more transitions, which is why the game was also more difficult for them."

This was an astute analysis of United's most recent game as well as their team this year.

As divisive as the phrase "United DNA" is, it undoubtedly remains a key part of the conversation about United both externally and internally.

This is because certain coaches have leaned into the club's roots, while others have tried but failed to move away from those ideas.

"We want to win; we want to be excited - that's why we love this club. I'm fully aware that we need to do it in a certain way," said Carrick when asked what style of football he wanted his United side to play.

Here he echoed the sentiment of United's most successful manager, Sir Alex Ferguson, who in 2017 said: "You have a duty to entertain. We have to always remember there's a public to be entertained."

With excitement seemingly non-negotiable for Ferguson, it is obvious why fans and players of that era resonate with a United that create spectacles.

Dynamic, direct and open games are sought after to remain connected to a United they recognise.

Solsjkaer's side embodied United's DNA before Ruben Amorim looked to play a more choreographed and risk-averse style of play. Carrick went back in the opposite direction.

Having established the context, we can take a closer look at how this has manifested on the pitch.

A side not built to break down low blocks

With the messaging around Carrick's style of play being one of proactivity, excitement and directness, it is no surprise that United look better with space to attack – something that happens more often for a team with less of the ball.

The strengths of the squad are suited to this approach, with goalkeeper Senne Lammens a good long kicker of the ball. In defenders Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez, United have punchy progressive passers from deep too.

In attack, Marcus Rashford is a willing runner in behind, often moving into a striker position despite starting on the wing. The same can be said for Bryan Mbeumo.

Bruno Fernandes, central to all of this, is a strong passer when attacking in transition, finding runners ahead of him – a role in which he broke the Premier League assist record last term.

Carrick has also provided certain players a level of freedom to make their own decisions on the pitch.

"Giving Bruno the platform to go and perform [has helped him]," Carrick said in April.

"We're trying to create a structure to try to bring out the best of everyone, but I like seeing Bruno in attacking positions with a bit of freedom."

Although players may enjoy this responsibility, how the team play can be swayed by individual players' natural tendencies.

With more risk-taking, direct passers in the side, when United are asked to disorganise stubborn defences their long-standing habits can mean losing the ball more often.

When dominating the ball, breaking down a team requires strong one-against-one wingers. Defending teams often clog the centre of the pitch, as City did in the derby, forcing the attacking side to the flank.

City's Jeremy Doku, Arsenal 's Bukayo Saka, Bayern Munich's Michael Olise and Paris St-Germain's Khvicha Kvaratskhelia have been key in helping those sides win often – while keeping the ball.

This season United have used a 4-2-4 shape in possession. The full-backs have pushed up and taken turns with the wingers to hold wide or narrow positions.

This, however, often results in Luke Shaw, Patrick Dorgu, Diogo Dalot and Mbeumo – not the strongest one-v-one dribblers - isolated on the wing.

Amorim used a system without wingers and the squad built as a result – with the exception of Rashford and Amad Diallo – appear underprepared to create chances from out wide.

With wide play an area of concern, play is often funnelled back infield.

Carrick has primarily used Fernandes and Matheus Cunha as a floating front two, both with licence to drop deep or pull wider.

Both players are more suited to facing the opposition's goal, rather than playing with their back to goal in small spaces, which makes it hard for United to capitalise through the middle.

City's Rayan Cherki and Arsenal 's Kai Havertz are players suited to this role, albeit in different ways.

Fernandes and Cunha's quality means they can still be effective in these positions, often forming triangles with the full-back and wingers, helping United get into the final third.

But as they both vacate the striker position, United end up lacking bodies in the box when they play crosses in.

The best teams have repeatable methods of chance creation in the final third that suit their players' strengths. Teams then cycle through these depending on what the opposition are offering them.

With United's attackers given more freedom, they often seem to be looking to solutions during the game more reactively compared to the more repeatable methods of creation Maresca can fall back on.

With United struggling to beat teams that allow them the ball, their impressive set-pieces provided them with a workaround last season.

Since Carrick took over, 56% of United's opening goals have come from corners, free-kicks or penalties, and 28% from Casemiro's headers.

After scoring, opponents are more likely to attack, which stretches the game, allowing United to play to their strengths and in a more direct fashion.

This season they have not shown that same prowess and, although Casemiro is known for his defending, the loss of his ability to help open the scoring makes United's attacking concerns against deep defences a more pressing issue to address.

articles.title: Vinicius responde a la afición del Elche por su cántico contra él: "¡Más, más, más... Cuidado!"
articles.standfirst: Las cámaras de Movistar captaron la reacción de Vinicius antes los cánticos del Martínez Valero
articles.summary: Las cámaras de Movistar captaron la reacción de Vinicius antes los cánticos del Martínez Valero
articles.body: Vinicius respondió los cánticos de un sector de la afición del estadio Martínez Valero durante el partido que el Real Madrid acabó ganando 2-3. Las cámaras de 'Movistar Plus Deportes' captaron las palabras que cruzó Vinicius con la grada mientras le cantaban "¡Vinicius balón de playa!". "Más, más, más... Cuidado...", le replica el delantero brasileño a la afición del Elche mientras les dedica gestos con la mano. Elche y Real Madrid saltaron al césped del Martínez Valero con camisetas de apoyo a Ceuta, con las excepciones de Mbappé, Vinicius y Konaté. Los tres recogieron sus camisetas con el lema "Todos somos caballas" (en apoyo explícito a la ciudad autónoma de Ceuta) en el túnel de vestuarios. Konaté se limitó a portar la camiseta en las manos, mientras que Mbappé y Vinicius salieron con ella sobre los hombros, pero sin acabar de desplegarla sobre su tronco más allá del pecho. Pero, ya en el pasamanos, ninguno de los dos la lució, un acto que llamó la atención. Tras el partido Vinicius Júnior reconoció que "no" puede "fallar tantas" ocasiones, pero esperó que "los goles van a volver". "Los goles van a volver… no puedo fallar tantas. Domingo hay más (el Real Madrid se mide al Atlético de Madrid en el estadio Metropolitano). ¡Hala Madrid!", publicó el delantero brasileño en su cuenta oficial de 'Instagram'. Vinicius jugó hasta el minuto 68 frente al Elche, con cinco remates, solo uno entre los tres palos y sin ningún gol.

articles.title: Raúl Varela: "Mourinho, por momentos, parece quedarse sin discurso"
articles.standfirst: El presentador de La Tribu cuestiona el funcionamiento del Real Madrid pese a la victoria ante el Elche: "¿Para qué vino Mourinho?"
articles.summary: El presentador de La Tribu cuestiona el funcionamiento del Real Madrid pese a la victoria ante el Elche: "¿Para qué vino Mourinho?"
articles.body: La victoria del Real Madrid ante el Elche no disipó las dudas de Raúl Varela sobre el funcionamiento del conjunto blanco. El presentador de La Tribu puso el foco en José Mourinho y, especialmente, en un problema que considera que se está repitiendo partido tras partido: el bajón del equipo durante las segundas partes. Varela comenzó mostrando su comprensión ante la posibilidad de que Mourinho reduzca el número de comparecencias ante los medios. "Estoy completamente de acuerdo con que José Mourinho debe saltarse alguna rueda de prensa de las que le programan cada semana. Seis son muchas", señaló. A partir de ahí, Varela comparó la situación actual con la primera etapa del portugués. "El caso es que ya sospecho por qué Mou quiere limitar su presencia ante unos medios que en esta segunda etapa solo le hablan de fútbol. Nada de The Special One, el dedo en el ojo o la lista de árbitros encabezada por el ínclito alemán Wolfgang Stark". Y lanzó una reflexión sobre el entrenador madridista: "Al Madrid lo que le falta es hablar más de la pelota y Mou, por momentos, parece quedarse sin discurso. ¿Para qué vino Mourinho?" Varela recordó además las expectativas que existían alrededor del equipo: "En realidad se nos dijo que la plantilla era de notable nivel y que con la llegada de los Diomandés, Bernardos, Konatés y compañía solo haría falta correr un poquito más y de forma ordenada. Pues siete partidos y siete calcos". El director de La Tribu señaló especialmente el rendimiento del Madrid después del descanso. "Si apagas la tele al descanso de los partidos pensarás que todo ha sido un paseo militar de un equipo tremendamente fallón de cara al marco contrario pero que controla lo que sucede en el campo". Sin embargo, para Varela, el escenario cambia en las segundas partes: "Normalmente lo del 'yo controlo' suele ser una mala idea y el accidente siempre ronda en la segunda parte en la que se vuelve un equipo irreconocible, perezoso, sin actitud, con desidia y en cierto modo hasta irrespetuoso con un rival como el Elche". El conjunto ilicitano llegó a igualar el encuentro antes de que el Madrid terminara llevándose la victoria. "Sin hacer nada más que intentar atacar por decoro te fuerza un empate que ayer bien pudo haber costado media liga", afirmó. Varela cerró su análisis señalando también la reacción del entrenador desde el banquillo: "Mou se pasó por la sala de prensa del Martínez Valero sin rechistar. Bastante tuvo con respirar y no tener que explicar porque le salió todo mal y no hizo apenas nada para remediarlo".
