articles.title: Leam Richardson ‘Very Proud’ Of Players After Brentford Cup Exit
articles.summary: The Royals put in a valiant effort but ultimately came up short against the top-flight Bees.
articles.body:
The Royals bowed out of the Carabao Cup following a 2-1 defeat against Premier League Brentford on Tuesday night.

In an entertaining contest, Reading can count themselves unfortunate not to have taken more from the game. The visitors made a quick start, taking the lead inside three minutes through Callum Wilson .

Paudie O'Connor thought he had levelled with a spectacular bicycle kick, only for the goal to be ruled out for a high boot. Brentford then doubled their advantage just before the break through Fabio Carvalho.

O'Connor did get his goal in the second half to give the Royals hope, but, despite pushing for a late equaliser, Reading were unable to find a way through.

Manager Leam Richardson was proud of his side's performance but was left frustrated with some decisions made by officials. Here's what he had to say when he spoke to Royals TV after the game.

"I think the first emotion is that I'm very proud of the players. Credit goes to the players with how they delivered themselves.

"We made a few changes. The lads have been working ever so hard and I thought they deserved that from the performance and the result in the last round, to go into this game.

"To be fair, we ran into a Premier League team who haven't been beaten, who had a really good result in the last round, and they didn't play with the handbrake on at all. They played their full squad, so to speak.

"But I thought we were value for a result and I thought the performance was really strong as well."

Richardson on conceding in the first three minutes

"It's not ideal, that, is it? I know it's a slip in the corner, but when you play against a Premier League team and they score after two or three minutes, you're trying to think how we can help the players on the pitch, how we can reconnect and go again.

"But I thought the response from the players was excellent. I thought we grew into the game and had a perfectly good goal scored, which I'm sure we're going to talk about.

"Overall, I'm very pleased and very proud of the players, very proud of the football club, but just disappointed with the result."

"Well, I've got to be honest, I think it's possibly in the top three worst decisions I've ever seen in football – and I've seen a lot of games, thousands of games, and I've played in a lot.

"I don't think Paudie scored one of those goals even when he was seven in his back garden! I'm not sure he'll score one again, so he's probably been robbed of his highlight reel.

"It's alright, we can laugh about it a little bit now, but we've come off the back of the weekend where we should get a penalty – a blatant penalty in my opinion and the lad must get sent off.

"Then, as we're growing into the game, we should go 1-1, in the ascendancy, with all the game to play. I have no idea why it's not given.

"I'd suggest everybody watches it and they can give me their opinion, because I'm really, really struggling for words for that one."

"I thought it was a blatant penalty. The lad's come out, slid out, his arms are out, a bit like a goalkeeper making a save, and the referee's looking right down at it.

"I don't really ever come on and criticise officials, you know that, but when it starts happening regularly, it starts becoming a bit of a problem.

"We've got to address it and we've got to address it quickly because our players work too hard and the fans pay too much money to make sure that we can get those simple decisions right. They should be getting them right.

"On another day, we'd probably have a different conversation, but because it's in the cup and it's a Premier League team, everything's, 'Oh, it's okay, we played well.'

"It's not right. It's not right. We should possibly be on the other side of the result because they're massive decisions. Massive decisions."

Richardson on moving forwards after the positive performance

"I think the level of performance in the last four or five games has been high. I think there's still a lot of growth in this squad and this team, as you've seen tonight, because the players are working really hard with myself, the coaches and the coaching staff daily. You can see it slowly coming out on the pitch.

"We're trying to adapt that and give more responsibility to the players on the pitch to lead a bit more and have that demand on each other, and you can see it slowly coming out.

"I think we'll get better as a team and we'll get better as a squad, because I thought there were some really good performances tonight, individually but, again, collectively against a really good, strong Premier League side."

"Yeah. At half-time, that was probably my only little criticism. Obviously the goal before half-time is something we can affect. It doesn't matter the level of opposition, we've got to be miles better than that. A little bit like Saturday, we've got to stop that at source.

"But at half-time I was a little bit like, we have got belief, but let's show our arrogance but in a good way. Let's have a little bit more belief.

"The Charlie Savage shot, every day I see him put that in the top corner. Technically excellent, but he just laid off it a little bit.

"There were a few moments where you have respect for your opposition all the time, but have respect for yourself and have a little bit more belief.

"I thought in the second half, and in the main, we had a lot of belief. We had some really good, strong moments and were really good in transition. Like you say, that was against some good opposition as well.

"So I'm very proud of the players tonight."

Richardson on the performances of players who have come in

"Excellent. It's what we expect. At the minute, there'll be certain players who are disappointed not to play regularly, but that's what squads are for. If you want to be successful, you've got to have a good squad and, whatever role you play at this moment in time, play it.

"You can control how you eat, how you sleep and how you train. They're professional footballers, so be professional and make sure that when you get your chance because in football it changes quickly.

"The world spins and then it's your moment, and you'll get all the support of everybody else, myself, the fans, the players and your teammates.

"They're in a good place at the minute. The lads who are pushing are pushing in the right way. Their attitude and their professionalism have been excellent, and it shows tonight because if you have really strong habits daily, they come out when you need them the most.

"Tonight we were stretched at times, which against Premier League opposition you're going to be, so you rely on those habits. I thought we had really strong habits tonight."

articles.title: La pértiga (otra vez)
articles.standfirst: Sobran los motivos, por Alberto R. Barbero
articles.summary: Sobran los motivos, por Alberto R. Barbero
articles.body: "No quiero que se entere el equipo contrario..." Tan fácil como eso. Cualquiera puede verlo y escucharlo a través de la televisión, incluido el rival. Un tipo toma nota, se pone en comunicación con el 'staff' en cuestión y la acción de un técnico encontrará enseguida la reacción del otro. Por eso Luis García Plaza se desesperaba el sábado, por eso Diego Pablo Simeone se ha desesperado tantas veces, por eso Antonio Hidalgo y tantos otros no dan una sola instrucción de carácter táctico hasta que no desaparece la pértiga... La famosa pértiga, la dichosa pértiga. A la que, acaba de comprobarlo el 'culpable' de ambas, ya se dedicó aquí una columna parecida hace un par de años. Entre que el problema no se resuelve y que falta creatividad... La cuestión, cuentan los que saben del tema, es que ese brazo telescópico que acerca el micrófono a la fuente del sonido, en este caso el entrenador, no tiene carácter obligatorio para los equipos, sino que forma parte de una serie de acciones incentivadas y remuneradas por la propia Liga. Si se acepta, dinerito; si no se acepta, pelillos a la mar. Pero eso no se lo han debido contar a los del banquillo. O se lo han contado y se hacen el longuis. Sigue siendo curioso que todo este guirigay llegue además bajo el paraguas de la pausa de hidratación, pero lo de España en ese sentido es lo de menos después de los míticos tres minutazos que se cascó la FIFA en el Mundial, tiempo suficiente para hidratarse, para dar instrucciones, incluso para echar un cigarro si se tercia, en definitiva para ciscarse en el fútbol de toda la vida. Un saludo para Duplantis, que seguramente nos estará leyendo.

articles.title: Real Madrid ready to approve Manchester United move for Endrick in January
articles.summary: Real Madrid could be busy in the winter transfer window, particularly when it comes to exits. The main issue at Valdebebas will inevitably surround Endrick,...
articles.body:
Real Madrid could be busy in the winter transfer window, particularly when it comes to exits. The main issue at Valdebebas will inevitably surround Endrick , who's had a difficult start to the 2026-27 campaign, given that he's barely featured.

His late cameo in Tuesday's last-gasp victory over Elche is the first minutes Endrick has had this season. Granted, he missed the first four matches due to injury, but even so, it looks difficult for him to play regularly under Jose Mourinho.

Endrick has Kylian Mbappe and Carlos Espi ahead of him in the striker pecking order, while Arda Guler , Yan Diomande and Brahim Diaz are currently preferred on the right wing. Thus, his chances of regular minutes are low, which is why there are chances for him to depart for the second winter transfer window in a row.

Real Madrid will re-assess Endrick's situation in the lead-up to January, and if he is still far down the pecking order, it's likely that another loan move will be sought. However, Manchester United would prefer to sign him permanently, and according to TEAMtalk (via CaughtOffside ), their long-term interest could materialise into a transfer offer when the window re-opens.

What should Real Madrid do with Endrick?

While it is true that Endrick showed a great level during his loan spell at Lyon last season, he has yet to make a significant impact at the Bernabeu since he joined Real Madrid in the summer of 2024. Club bosses are still being patient, but that patience could start to run thin if he fails to establish himself under Mourinho.

There is a world in which Real Madrid allow Endrick to leave permanently, and Man United would be primed to strike if that happens. However, they would surely look to include a sell-on clause and/or buy-back clause, as this would allow them to retain control over his future.

articles.title: Federico Valverde celebrates 250 La Liga appearances for Real Madrid after Elche win: ‘Want to keep winning more titles’
articles.summary: Federico Valverde reached another landmark in a Real Madrid shirt on Tuesday, making his 250th La Liga appearance for the club during the 3-2 victory over El...
articles.body:
Federico Valverde reached another landmark in a Real Madrid shirt on Tuesday, making his 250th La Liga appearance for the club during the 3-2 victory over Elche at the Martinez Valero.

The milestone arrived on a night when Madrid had to dig deep after surrendering a two-goal advantage, eventually securing victory through a late Carlos Espi goal.

For Valverde, though, the occasion carried significance beyond the result.

"You never imagine you'll reach this milestone, or achieve so much. I've achieved so much here.

"I want to keep winning more titles and continue making history at this club, leave my mark and make my name known at this great club, the best in the world.

"For me, it's an honour and a great source of satisfaction to keep achieving these things, to keep delivering for the team, and as long as the team wins, I'm happy," he told Real Madrid TV .

Valverde proud of Real Madrid's response

Valverde made his 250th La Liga appearance for Real Madrid. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

The Uruguay international was pleased with much of what he saw from Real Madrid, particularly their first-half performance, despite the uncomfortable finish.

"We're delighted with the victory. We played one of our best first halves of the season.

"We're happy with the result and to be back to winning ways. We're happy for my teammates because I think they played a very good match and, above all, the goalscorers were there when they needed to be."

Yan Diomande was another talking point after the victory, with Valverde encouraged by what he has seen from the youngster.

"We're still getting to know Diomande. He's a player who possesses all the qualities needed when moving forward to take on defenders and in one-on-one situations.

"I have faith in him; we all have faith in him. I knew he'd have the chance to provide an assist or score, and he ended up with a spectacular pass to Mbappe."

Valverde already looking towards Atletico

Valverde is already looking forward to the Madrid derby. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

For Real Madrid, there is little time to savour the Elche victory, with the Madrid derby against Atletico coming at the weekend.

"We need to be in good shape for the derby at the weekend. This win gives us a huge boost, some positive energy, and now it's time to rest and prepare for the next match.

"We're excited, raring to go and full of energy. It was important to win so we'd be in good spirits going into the next match.

"We're happy with the victory, with how the team is performing, and with how the lads took to the pitch.

"The substitutes are very important to us. Today they turned the match around," he concluded.

articles.title: Atletico Madrid have promised to lower Barcelona target Julian Alvarez’s release clause on one condition – report
articles.summary: Julian Alvarez was the most talked-about player in the transfer market this past summer, as his bid to force a move to Barcelona failed sensationally, with t...
articles.body:
Julian Alvarez was the most talked-about player in the transfer market this past summer, as his bid to force a move to Barcelona failed sensationally, with the player ending up remaining at Atletico Madrid , against his own will.

The relations between Alvarez and the club remain tense, but the attacker has featured in three matches so far, notably playing the entire ninety minutes against Liverpool.

The key factor that prevented Barcelona from signing him was his hefty €500 million release clause that the Catalans had to meet.

Alvarez's future at Atleti hangs in the balance. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

However, with Alvarez's future still under doubt, Atletico Madrid appear willing to reduce his release clause.

According to El Chiringuito , Atletico Madrid president Gil Marin has promised Alvarez that the value of his release clause will be lowered but only on one condition.

The striker has to score at least 20 goals this season. One might think this will not be an issue for the Argentine, given that he scored 20 goals last season in all competitions and 29 goals in his debut campaign for Atleti.

What this does mean, however, is that Atleti only see Alvarez as potentially leaving at the end of the season and not necessarily in the upcoming January transfer window.

What's in store for Alvarez's future? (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images)

Given the magnanimous start that Barcelona have enjoyed to the season so far, it is perhaps easy to dismiss the need for someone like Julian Alvarez .

Barcelona, after all, are the most prolific team in Europe right now, with the combination of Raphinha and Lamine Yamal scoring goals for fun.

But in hindsight, the Catalans could use the services of someone like Alvarez, who can not only provide an additional edge to the attack but also reduce the burden on Yamal and Raphinha.

Although the two players are performing brilliantly right now, any potential injury could drastically hamper Barcelona's quality in front of goal.

Therefore, the club should take any market opportunity they can in order to get their hands on Alvarez, either in January or next summer.

articles.title: Leverkusen boss Martinez confirms goalkeeping choice for European nights
articles.summary: Carles Martinez confirmed Mark Flekken will also start Europa League games for Bayer Leverkusen as Janis Blaswich has to wait for DFB-Pokal action. The 33-ye...
articles.body:
Carles Martinez confirmed Mark Flekken will also start Europa League games for Bayer Leverkusen as Janis Blaswich has to wait for DFB-Pokal action. The 33-year-old conceded five goals in Leverkusen's first two away games in the Bundesliga.

"As for the goalkeeper, I have decided that Mark (Flekken) will play on Wednesday," the Catalan said in the pre-match conference for the game against NK Celje. The former Toulouse boss had previously left his goalkeeping choice for the Europa League open.

"Mistakes are part of football. That's something I firmly believe in. If someone makes a mistake, that's no reason to say, 'come on, you're out!'" Martinez added after Flekken's weekend performance drew more criticism.

"I think he's a great professional. He's doing incredible things. He's the first one to be there. He's the first to push for us to get better as a squad. So I am very satisfied in many ways. My philosophy is to stand by my players, especially after mistakes," Martinez reiterated his trust in the former Freiburg shot-stopper.

When Leverkusen competed in the Europa League during Xabi Alonso's spell, Matěj Kovář was the preferred choice for all cup games, while Lukas Hradecky was the starting goalkeeper in the Bundesliga.

Leverkusen's European campaign will start at home against Slovenian side NK Celje. Apart from games against Ligue sides Marseille (MD04) and Lyon (MD08), they will face teams outside the top-five leagues in the league phase of Europe's secondary competition.

articles.title: Un 'niño' de Mourinho en el banquillo de Mourinho
articles.standfirst: Álvaro López, excanterano al que el portugués hizo debutar en 2012, será el técnico que ocupará su sitio en el Bernabéu el sábado para dirigir al Madrid en la Intercontinental sub 20
articles.summary: Álvaro López, al que el portugués hizo debutar con el primer equipo, será el técnico que se sentará en el Bernabéu para dirigir al Madrid en la final de la Intercontinental sub 20
articles.body: Un 'niño' de Mourinho en el sitio de Mourinho. El banquillo del Madrid en el Bernabéu tendrá inquilino nuevo por un día. Será el sábado durante la Intercontinental sub 20 que el Madrid, como campeón de la Youth League, disputará ante el Santiago Wanderers, ganador de la Libertadores de la categoría. Álvaro López, excanterano blanco al que el portugués hizo debutar con el primer equipo en 2012, será el técnico que se siente en el Bernabéu para dirigir al combinado sub 20 de La Fábrica que afrontarán la gran final. Álvaro López, viejo conocido de Mou, hará de Mou. Mourinho puede estar tranquilo porque 'su' banquillo del Bernabéu está en buenas manos. Aquel canterano al que hizo debutar en un amistoso en Oviedo se ha convertido en la sensación de La Fábrica como técnico tras lograr la pasada temporada un histórico triplete con el Juvenil A, conquistando Youth League, Liga y Copa de Campeones. La reconquista de Europa es lo que ha llevado al Madrid a disputar la Intercontinental sub 20 por primera vez y optar a convertirse en la mejor Fábrica del mundo. La pasada temporada fue de ensueño para Álvaro López, que firmó una espectacular cuenta de resultados de 37 victorias en los 41 partidos que dirigió entre Juvenil A y Juvenil C. Arrancó la campaña en el banquillo del tercer juvenil con un pleno de 15 victorias en 15 partidos y en los cinco meses que estuvo al frente del Juvenil A, tras su ascenso a principios de año, fueron 22 victorias en 26 partidos. Si sumamos la temporada 24-25, donde lideró desde el banquillo el recital del Cadete A de la 'Generación 2009' en el campeonato liguero (29 victorias y un empate), más las tres victorias que lleva esta temporada (dos en Liga y una en Youth) el balance de Álvaro López es de 69 victorias en los últimos 74 partidos oficiales que ha dirigido. Álvaro López lleva toda una vida en La Fábrica. A sus 35 años, dos décadas las ha pasado en Valdebebas. Primero fue una joya de la cantera como jugador y ahora lo es como entrenador. El mismo impacto que está teniendo en el banquillo lo tuvo en su momento en el césped, siendo uno de los jugadores de mayor proyección de la generación del 91, que junto a la del 92 revolucionaron La Fábrica como una de las 'cosechas' más productivas de la historia. Carvajal, Álex Fernández, Sarabia, Lucas Vázquez, Álvaro Morata, Óscar Plano, Pacheco, Fran Sol, Rubén Sobrino, Rodrigo Moreno… Y Álvaro López. Antes de que las lesiones frenaran su proyección y le obligasen a una retirada prematura, Álvaro López tuvo una gran trayectoria como futbolista. Fue un mediocentro brillante y talentoso. "Era nuestro timón, capital y capitán. Era un jugador con muchas posibilidades, mediocentro moderno, tipo Busquets", recordaba Alberto Toril de él. El técnico con el que se coronó campeón de la Copa de Campeones juvenil en 2010 ante el Valencia de Isco y compartiendo equipo con Carvajal, Sarabia, Fran Sol y Lucas Vázquez, entre otros. Luego llegaría su debut con el Castilla en la 10-11 y se convertiría en 'niño' de Mourinho, que lo hizo debutar con el primer equipo en un amistoso ante el Oviedo en 2012. El técnico portugués no sólo le marcó por eso, también por una breve charla entre ellos que guarda en secreto como oro paño en el baúl de sus recuerdos como futbolista. Con la selección ganó el Europeo sub 17 que España conquistó en 2008 y fue titular junto a Thiago Alcántara en la final ante Francia, un baño histórico inolvidable (0-4). También fue internacional sub 19 a las órdenes de Luis Milla. Tras un breve recorrido lejos del Madrid, Álvaro López comenzó a labrarse su futuro ya sin las botas puestas. Se licenció en Publicidad y RRPP por la UCM y se sacó un master de Dirección de Comunicación en Empresas. Pero el fútbol no tardó en volver a llamar a su puerta e inicio su carrera en los banquillos. En la temporada 18-19 se estrenó como entrenador en La Fábrica al frente del alevín B y pronto empezó a llamar la atención. El Madrid lo eligió como 'escudero' de Arbeloa en el debut en los banquillos del ahora técnico del Fulham en la 20-21 al frente del Infantil A. Aquel año ganó la Liga y se ganó a Arbeloa. "No puedo tener más que palabras de agradecimiento hacia un profesional intachable, con talento, liderazgo e ilusión. He disfrutado y aprendido mucho a tu lado", fue el mensaje que Arbeloa le dedicó Álvaro al final de la temporada. Álvaro López seguiría su camino como técnico en La Fábrica y pronto empezó a acumular éxitos. En la 22-23 ganó la Promise con el Alevín A y también la Liga, tras 29 victorias y un empate y marcando 161 goles. En la 23-24 también se coronó campeón de Liga y volvió a superar el listón de los cien goles. La 24-25 fue un punto de inflexión porque puso en órbita a la que es posiblemente una de las generaciones que cuenta con mayores expectativas en el club junto a la de 2007. Se trata de la de 2009, la de los Enzo Alves, Company, Lemaitre, Mateo Garrido, Yeremaiah, Bugarín, Guille Ponce, Del Pino o Raúl Andrei. Un grupo de joyas a la que Álvaro López encumbró siendo cadetes tras una temporada espectacular en la que arrasaron en Liga y conquistaron dos de los torneos internacionales más prestigiosos de la categoría: en febrero lograron el torneo Al Kass tras ganar 3-0 al PSG en la final y en junio ganaron el torneo Al Abtal Cup goleando 5-2 al Barcelona en la final. El Madrid promocionaría a esta brillante generación de jugadores y también al técnico. Álvaro López ascendió al Juvenil C y poco después al Juvenil A, que dirige desde el pasado mes de enero. A sus órdenes, el tercer filial blanco revolucionó La Fábrica con un triplete para la historia, ganando Youth League, Liga y Copa de Campeones en un año mágico e inolvidable.

articles.title: La Europa League impulsa al Getafe hacia su mayor presupuesto desde 2020
articles.standfirst: El club de LaLiga EA Sports vuelve a la Europa League con una cifra de negocio de 66,7 millones
articles.summary: El club de LaLiga EA Sports vuelve a la Europa League con una cifra de negocio de 66,7 millones
articles.body: El EuroGeta presenta su gasolina para viajar por el continente. El Getafe CF vuelve a la Europa League y lo hace con fuerza en la parcela económica. Sólo de negocio ordinario prevé facturar 66,7 millones en 2026-2027, un 18% más interanual y sin computar en esta suma los variables por su rendimiento en el segundo torneo europeo y el ticketing que pueda obtener en el mismo, según se desprende del presupuesto del equipo azulón, al que ha tenido acceso 2Playbook. Si se revisa su última participación en esta competición, en 2019-2020, entonces obtuvo unos 10 millones por estas dos vías, lo que dibuja una facturación ordinaria que podría superar los 75 millones a cierre de ejercicio si no se producen grandes alteraciones respecto al presupuesto. En aquella ocasión, el equipo de José Bordalás llegó a octavos de final y obtuvo 15 millones de ingresos UEFA y otro medio millón por ticketing generado con las grandes noches europeas en el Coliseum. Entre el resto de partidas, destaca el descenso en la televisión de LaLiga, ligado principalmente a la devolución de los fondos de CVC (Plan Impulso), de los que el club ha tirado, por ejemplo, para la profunda reforma de su estadio. La modernización del estadio también debería ayudar a llegar al millón de euros con la taquilla. A ello se suman otros 2,9 millones por socios y abonados, un 6% más respecto a la previsión de 2025-2026. Por derechos audiovisuales se anota 56,3 millones, un 20% más respecto al presupuesto de 2025-2026. De este importe, 50,3 millones corresponden a LaLiga. Las cuentas de esta última temporada todavía no son públicas. Una partida con gran potencial para el conjunto azulón es la comercial. Ya en el presupuesto dibuja unos ingresos de 7 millones, un 12% más que en las previsiones de la temporada pasada. A fin de curso se conocerá si acuerdos recientes como el de Gree y otros se imputan ya ahí o aumentará la cifra. Por ahora, tiene garantizados los patrocinios principales de Tecnocasa (frontal de la camiseta) y Joma (socio técnico). A estas dos marcas de largo recorrido en la entidad se han sumado en el último año y medio otras como Mapei y Grand Class. En 2024 entró Lowi en la trasera de la camiseta dentro de su rally de patrocinios en clubes de LaLiga. La vuelta a Europa también eleva la inversión del club que preside y controla Ángel Torres. Una inversión que va, principalmente, a la parcela deportiva. En el primer presupuesto remitido a LaLiga antes del verano se dijo que la masa salarial iba a rondar los 41,4 millones de euros, de los que 32,6 millones eran sueldos del primer equipo. A ello se sumaban otros 5,2 millones en salarios no deportivos, con un incremento del 17% respecto al presupuesto de 2025-2026. Las amortizaciones por fichajes siguen a la baja, con 7,5 millones de euros fijados en ese presupuesto inicial, que igual que los salarios deportivos se desconoce si esta cifra ha evolucionado durante el periodo estival. Sea como fuere, el límite salarial que ha fijado LaLiga a los clubes para esta temporada, anunciado la semana pasada, le marca un tope de 56,7 millones de euros al equipo del sur de Madrid. Por último, las plusvalías por traspasos van al alza gracias a las ventas de Mauro Arambarri y Luis Milla. En total, el club se anota 21,5 millones ingresados esta temporada por la venta de futbolistas, lo que deja un beneficio neto de 9,5 millones por esta vía. Con todo ello, el Getafe confía en cerrar el ejercicio en positivo. De cumplir con el presupuesto, el club generaría un beneficio de 8,1 millones de euros, si bien en las últimas temporadas el cierre del ejercicio no ha coincidido con la previsión inicial. De hecho, el equipo madrileño acumula unas pérdidas de 23,6 millones entre su última participación en la Europa, en 2019-2020, y 2025-2026.

articles.title: Why Man United could be handed chance to sign Endrick from Real Madrid in January
articles.summary: 1Manchester United’s underwhelming start to the 2026/27 campaign could tempt them to return to the transfer market in the winter. The Red Devils have just on...
articles.body:
Manchester United's underwhelming start to the 2026/27 campaign could tempt them to return to the transfer market in the winter. The Red Devils have just one win in their first four Premier League games and are languishing in 13th place in the league table.

The English giants were outstanding under Michael Carrick in the second half of last season and were expected to hit a higher gear after a summer of investment. United spent over £150 million to refurbish their midfield, bringing in Andrey Santos , Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba .

A new left-back was on the agenda all summer, but the Red Devils also wanted to add more firepower to their attack to cover for Benjamin Sesko . Several candidates were considered for the job from the Premier League and abroad.

One of them was Real Madrid 's Endrick , who has been on United's wish list for a while and had struggled for prominence at the Santiago Bernabeu last season.

Endrick's struggles at the Santiago Bernabeu

Endrick has failed to nail down a regular place in the starting XI since arriving at the Santiago Bernabeu in the summer of 2024. The Brazilian managed seven goals and one assist in 37 appearances in all competitions under former manager Carlo Ancelotti.

However, Endrick struggled for prominence under the Italian's successor, Xabi Alonso, managing just three appearances in the first half of last season. The young striker ultimately decided to leave on loan in January, and United were among the clubs interested.

The Brazilian went on to join Lyon on a six-month deal and was very impressive in Ligue 1. Endrick registered eight goals and eight assists from 21 appearances, prompting renewed interest in his signature this summer.

The Red Devils were linked once again at the end of last season, but the player ended up staying at the Santiago Bernabeu. However, it now appears that the English giants could have the chance to prise him away at the turn of the year.

According to AS , Endrick was close to joining AS Roma this summer, but was convinced to stay by new manager Jose Mourinho. The report states: "Endrick had all but sealed his move to Roma during the last transfer window, aware that opportunities at Real Madrid would be few and far between in this new phase, particularly following the signing of Yan Diomande by the Whites."

"But José Mourinho intervened and asked that the Brazilian not leave the club; he was very pleased with his performance in pre-season and felt he could be very useful, particularly whilst Rodrygo is still recovering (which is not expected to be until January 2027)."

If the Brazilian was hoping for a regular run in the team this season, he has been left disappointed. Endrick has been afforded just four minutes of first-team action this season, although he did miss the first four games of the season with a muscle injury.

However, the arrival of Yan Diomande, coupled with Carlos Espi, Arda Guler and Brahim Diaz 's good form, has seen the 20 year old drop further down the pecking order at the Santiago Bernabeu. With Kylian Mbappe and Vinicius Junior also in the mix, Endrick's situation may not improve in the coming months.

That could open the door for a departure in the winter, so United could have the opportunity to secure his signature if they so desire. The report adds: "Endrick took the manager's word for it and stayed… and since then, nothing has gone the way he expected."

"He did so knowing that if things didn't work out, he could reassess his situation in January and go out on loan, as he did last season with that successful loan spell at Lyon that took him all the way to the World Cup."

United have scored 11 goals in their five games this season, but failed to find the back of the net against Manchester City as well as Hull City in the Premier League. As such, the Red Devils could be tempted to make a move for Endrick in January if he becomes available.

articles.title: WSL: Jana Fernandez signs new London City Lionesses contract
articles.summary: London City Lionesses defender Jana Fernandez signs a new contract, keeping her at the club until 2029.
articles.body:
London City Lionesses defender Jana Fernandez has signed a new contract, keeping her at the club until 2029.

The 24-year-old has become a key player for Eder Maestre’s side since joining from Barcelona a year ago.

She played in every Women’s Super League match for London City last season as they finished sixth in their debut campaign in the top flight.

Her performances at right-back earned her the fans’ votes for club player of the season.

"I'm absolutely delighted to sign a new contract here at London City," said Fernandez.

"When I arrived in England one year ago I joined this club with dreams for the future.

"Potential, excitement and progress are three words I associate with the club and I'm pleased to commit my future. I feel at home and settled here.

"We are building something special together, as players, staff and fans, and I can't wait to play my part."

Before her move to England, Fernandez spent her career at Barcelona, graduating from their academy and becoming a five-time league champion.

She also won the Champions League and Copa de la Reina three times.

Fernandez was part of the Spain team that finished runners-up to England at Euro 2025.

She has been joined at London City by former Barcelona team-mates Alexia Putellas - the two-time Ballon d'Or winner - and Mapi Leon.

Under US billionaire owner Michele Kang, London City hope to break into the WSL's traditional top three and qualify for the Champions League.

Having attracted big names in the summer, it was crucial London City retained their other talent, and they have been able to do that with Fernandez and England winger Freya Godfrey committing their futures in recent months.

articles.title: Thomas Tuchel: England boss on World Cup reflections, wishing he'd eaten Azteca grass and an 'exciting' future
articles.summary: The FA have released a documentary called Reflections: England's World Cup Journey; Three Lions boss Thomas Tuchel looks back on the summer campaign and explains how it has bonded him and the group for the upcoming Nations League and Euro 2028 challenges
articles.body:
That's just one of the statements from the England boss which has drawn attention across social media, following the FA releasing a new documentary called 'Reflections: England's World Cup Journey'.

In the documentary, Tuchel sits alongside former England international and Sky Sports pundit Daniel Sturridge to look back on England's campaign, which ultimately saw the team finish third, having lost in the semi-finals to Argentina.

England's standout performance of the tournament came in the last-16 win over Mexico in Mexico City, where they played for over 35 minutes with 10 men but prevailed 3-2.

"I texted a friend after the match and I just wrote, 'I regret that I didn't eat some grass after the match to keep something from this in my body forever'," said Tuchel.

On the unity his players showed in that match, Tuchel pointed to their reaction to Jordan Henderson falling and breaking his arm in the post-match celebrations.

"If you needed any proof, any proof for what it meant to these players and how they were with each other, it was the moment when Jordan fell over and broke his arm," said Tuchel.

"Within a second, the players were there, every single player was there, stopping the celebrations, building a shield, protecting Jordan and not going nowhere in full empathy. It was just so special."

The film will be released on Wednesday September 16 exclusively on the England app.

The build-up to the Mexico game had been dominated by talk of the altitude of the Azteca stadium but also the potential for weather delays, which proved founded with kick-off pushed back.

But Tuchel says a calm came over the group when they trained together in Mexico before the match and meditation and manifestation helped them to achieve the victory.

"In the middle of Mexico City and we arrived and it's an oasis, it's so peaceful, it's an unbelievable pitch and it is so calm, it is so peaceful that it did something to the players," said Tuchel.

"They came out from the gym straight out on the pitch, they were having phone calls, walking around, it was such a peaceful energy.

"So we came up with this line of 'silence is powerful', that we enjoy the silence, we're in a home country, we will play against the whole nation, the whole nation will be against us, the stadium, it's almost impossible to win in the stadium, no one has ever done it before in a World Cup match.

"So let's enjoy the silence, the power of the silence. We even had five minutes on the match day of meditation and manifestation of the last whistle."

The FA are currently undergoing a review of England's World Cup campaign but Tuchel says the experience has bonded him and the group together and he is "excited" about what comes next.

England face world champions Spain in the Nations League in the upcoming international break with the 2028 Euros the next major tournament. Tuchel reckons preparing for that tournament will be easier than the planning which was required for the 2026 World Cup.

"It created a huge bond to these players, it feels like they are my players now. This is the beauty of it," said Tuchel.

"When you have a manager and then you have success and you have painful moments together, but you have so much time together and then you create a natural bond.

"I'm happy to see them, I'm happy to challenge them, happy to push them and very proud to be a part of them.

"I'm very excited. I'm excited to work with these players. I'm excited to have new, young players that we can bring into camp and that they can learn.

"We've got another step closer and I think we're there.

"It's very difficult to prepare a World Cup in the US, but it's possible to prepare for a Euros and be prepared in Nations League tier one.

"The target is to have another 10 matches. We had 10 matches in the US, eight wins, one draw, one painful loss, but that is something to build on.

"We have all the right to hold our heads high and go with courage and positivity into the next challenges.

"We have four matches in the Nations League coming up and that's where the focus is."

Tuchel on Harry Kane going to another level

"Just so easy. He's always there, he's always in training, he always wants to train. The level to which he got himself now, since he's at Bayern Munich.

"The level of commitment and training, how he arrived in prep camp, how he arrived in the qualification matches, the speech after the October camp, and he straight away stood up in the dressing room and said, 'guys, we will keep on going in November, this is what we do'.

"He found another level in his game, but also as a personality, and how he shows up for training, how he drives training standards is one of a kind. The finishing is out of control good."

On Jude Bellingham living up to his full potential

"He was one of the players of the tournament, not only for us, but of the whole tournament.

"He lived up to his full potential, you could just see what a competitor, what a machine he is, and he just thrives on the pressure. He just loves these moments, he loves these stages, it brings out the very best.

"He came with an amazing mindset into camp, with the best physical preparation. He came fresh, he came hungry, hungry for football, hungry for minutes into camp. He took his place and decided every single match for us."

On the England fans and their 'special' connection with the team

"They lived up to the high expectations.

"Everyone told me, 'wait until the tournament starts, we will have the best fans, we will be right on top, it will be amazing, the amount of people…' and it was just like that from the first moment.

"They just felt this team. I believe that fans have a sense, maybe they cannot name it, someone will say, 'yeah, they give everything, they're sweating, after the whistle goes, they have to sit down because they're so tired'. For everyone it's maybe different, they feel it, they could sense it, that this team is together and this team means it.

"That's what made the connection so strong. That was not artificial. That was very special."

articles.title: Lionel Messi set for Argentina farewell in October 6 friendly against Benin
articles.summary: Messi will make his 208th and final appearance in the ‘farewell he truly deserves’, says Argentina football’s chief.
articles.body:
Lionel Messi was named in Argentina’s squad for a friendly against Benin on October 6, a match that will serve as his farewell appearance after announcing his international retirement last month.

The 39-year-old said in August he was retiring from Argentina duty after a two-decade international career that included winning the 2022 World Cup and Copa America triumphs in 2021 and 2024.

“We made the decision to invite the best player in the world, the symbol of our national team, our captain, Lionel Andres Messi, so that he can have the farewell he truly deserves on October 6 here in Argentina,” said the country’s FA president Claudio Tapia.

The match against Benin will take place at River Plate’s Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires, which can accommodate 85,000 spectators.

Tapia also invited all of Argentina’s 2022 World Cup winners to join Messi for what he said would be an “unforgettable” occasion.

Argentina begin a series of three friendlies against Bolivia on September 30 in Cordoba — their first match since losing the World Cup final to Spain — before taking on Burkina Faso in Buenos Aires on October 3.

Messi has been included in the squad for the third match against Benin, when he is expected to make his 208th and final appearance for the national team. He is Argentina’s all-time record scorer with 125 goals.

Following the death of his father Jorge last month, Messi had said he had “serious doubts” about continuing to play football of any sort for “much longer”.

“It was a decision that hurt and still hurts deep in my soul but I understand that it is the right time,” Messi said when he called time on his Argentina career.

His contract with Major League Soccer club Inter Miami runs until the end of the 2028 season.

Last month FIFA ordered Argentina to play their next home match with capacity reduced to 50 percent for breaches of its disciplinary code relating to using a sports event for making demonstrations of a non-sporting nature.

After Argentina beat England 2-1 in a tense World Cup semifinal in July, several players held up a banner saying: “The Falklands are Argentine”.

The friendlies are also expected to count towards suspensions handed down following incidents after Argentina’s World Cup final defeat by Spain.

Midfielder Leandro Paredes received a 10-match ban , while defender Nahuel Molina was suspended for seven games and Thiago Almada for one.

articles.title: 2026 College Football Fanbases That Should be Worried after Week 2
articles.summary: Can we have a do-over?
articles.body:
Two weeks into the season, you know this refrain is echoing through some football programs. Some teams are reeling at 0-2. Others are already colossal disappointments underachieving.

Then there are others who have an undefeated record written on paper. With a pencil. Just ready to be erased if they don't play much better real quickly.

Proud powerhouses, bottom-dwellers hoping things will change and some programs with new coaches have all experienced early-season letdowns. For most of them, at least, there's still time to turn things around.

If you're fans of these programs, it may be time to start counting down the days to basketball season.

Arkansas football fans have to be wondering if they're ever going to be good again.

The basketball program is on firm footing again with John Calipari at the helm, but football has been a revolving door of futility. From Bret Bielema to Chad Morris to Sam Pittman to Bobby Petrino, it's been bad and ugly.

The Razorbacks' coaching search zeroed in on Ryan Silverfield, who never really quite reached the level at Memphis that Mike Norvell did before him. Now, he's trying to build a program in the SEC arms race.

Last week, Silverfield got his first look at big-time football following a season-opening win against North Alabama. It was rough. The Hogs traveled to Utah and limped back after a 43-10 loss that could have been much worse.

No. 2-ranked Georgia follows this week, and if you look at that SEC schedule, it's extremely tough to find even a single win. If that's the case, Silverfield is going to be off to yet another forgettable start.

It's going to be an uphill battle to turn around the program in Fayetteville.

Every year, it's becoming more and more obvious the game has passed Dabo Swinney by.

The Clemson coach refuses to embrace the transfer portal. Teams all around him are lapping him. Swinney's stubborn pride is keeping the Tigers from remaining competitive in the new era. Right now, he's holding the proud program hostage.

If he doesn't adapt soon, the program is going to have to make the difficult decision to part ways with the legend.

Clemson was a top-five preseason team last year and limped to a 7-6 record. This year, it opened by getting absolutely obliterated by LSU in a game Lane Kiffin said was less competitive than when the Bayou Bengals' scout team simulated the other set of Tigers.

Playing backup quarterback Tait Reynolds against Georgia Southern, Clemson only beat the Eagles 22-7.

This year's rendition of Clemson looks like a bad football team so far. It might get uglier soon.

Maybe at this point, Florida State fans aren't exactly "worried." Maybe they want it to get bad enough to just end the Mike Norvell era, even though it's going to cost the school a lot of money.

It's been really bad for a really long time (relatively speaking) for a program used to winning big during the Bobby Bowden – and, to an extent, the Jimbo Fisher – era. Three years ago, the 'Noles were 13-1 and left out of the playoffs after Jordan Travis's season-ending injury.

They haven't been the same since Georgia torched them in the bowl game. FSU went 2-10 in 2024 and 5-7 last year. This season, they're 1-1, with a close loss to SMU, but they didn't look great in the season-opening 34-17 win over New Mexico State either.

Norvell's roster construction has been abysmal the past two years, highlighted by his inability to get the right portal quarterback (from DJ Uiagalelei to Thomas Castellanos to, now, Ashton Daniels).

A trip to Alabama this week probably won't bring with it any warm-and-fuzzies about the program, either, though Norvell's 'Noles did beat the Tide a season ago.

It feels like a matter of "when," not "if," the Norvell era ends.

Top QB Report Card Grades after Week 2 📝

Brent Key's Georgia Tech football program is built on toughness. So far, through an 0-2 start, that's been nonexistent.

The coach called out his Yellow Jackets for being "soft" after a stunning 14-13 loss to Colorado in Atlanta to open the season. The Buffaloes blocked a would-be game-winning field goal to win.

Things didn't get easier when Tennessee came to town in Week 2. While things were better on both sides of the ball, the Ramblin' Wreck wilted in the second half in a 45-24 loss. Key told ESPN television reporters heading into a two-score fourth quarter that he challenged his team.

That challenge fell flat as the Vols scored 14 points to pull away.

Perhaps the worst thing for the Yellow Jackets is that both losses were at home. Those were golden opportunities to make some national noise. Instead, a rebuilt team that traded quarterback Haynes King for Alberto Mendoza and grabbed Michigan RB Justice Haynes from the portal is trying to find itself.

It may be a rebuilding season for the Wreck.

Brent Venables has 10 wins in two of his four seasons as Oklahoma's head coach, but in case you forgot, there was some hot-seat talk prior to the 2025 campaign.

The Sooners reeled off a late-season run that ended in the College Football Playoff. That made aspirations even higher this year. They are used to winning on a national scale. Just because OU is now in the deep, rugged SEC doesn't change its program standards.

Last weekend's 17-10 loss at Michigan, though, is a huge red flag.

Quarterback John Mateer may get more unwarranted hype than any other quarterback in the country. Even though he is a tough player, he's always been a limited passer. That reared its head again in Ann Arbor. The Sooners don't have enough weapons around Mateer, but the fact is, the senior can't consistently get them the ball, anyway.

When you factor in how the offensive line got dominated against the Wolverines, there are several causes for concern when you look ahead to a schedule that includes No. 2 Georgia, No. 1 Texas, No. 8 Ole Miss, No. 9 Texas A&M, and No. 20 Missouri.

South Carolina, Kentucky and Mississippi State aren't gimmes, either. This could be an interesting year in Norman.

Coach Dan Lanning's team is a straight-up mess right now. No amount of lip service is going to change that fact.

Quarterback Dante Moore appears to have regressed early in the season after nearly being a top-five NFL draft pick a season ago. Offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer hasn't been able to recapture the magic left behind by Will Stein, who is now Kentucky's head coach.

While the Ducks have as much defensive talent as anybody, they're allowing 33 points per game during a 1-1 start that saw them barely beat Boise State and lose to an Oklahoma State team that became the first team in history to snap at least a 10-game losing streak by beating a top-10 team.

This is a team that is capable of turning it around at any time to still make it to the College Football Playoff, but they've not looked anything like a team that has that in them yet. What a downer of a start for a team many thought would win the Natty.

Rutgers will never be mistaken for a juggernaut, but the Scarlet Knights haven't been terrible in Greg Schiano's second stint in New Jersey.

Though they didn't make a bowl game a season ago, they finished 5-7 after a pair of seven-win seasons. For the state university, that's a pretty solid stretch. It's been tough sledding since joining the Big Ten, but Schiano at least had them back to a respectable program.

This season feels like a monumental step backward.

Rutgers made national news in Week 1 when a UMass team that went winless a season ago dominated the Scarlet Knights in a 37-21 win.

Just when you thought maybe they were stunned, and it couldn't be that bad, they went on the road last week and could have beaten Boston College, but threw four interceptions on their way to a 28-21 loss.

That's likely the worst ACC team Rutgers fell to. They likely won't be favored in any of their remaining games except against Howard.

Moving to a Power Four conference isn't ever easy, but some teams (like SMU) may make it look that way. Others, like UCF and Cincinnati, have been middling since the move.

Since joining the Big 12, UCF is 7-21 in league play and just 16-23 overall.

They traded Gus Malzahn for Scott Frost a season ago, hoping Frost could rekindle the magic he had as the Knights' head coach that culminated in an unbeaten season and a (mythical) national championship. Frost bolted for his alma mater in Nebraska. He flamed out and is now back in Orlando.

It's been far from a smooth run. After last week's 12-7 loss to Pittsburgh, where the Knights couldn't muster any offense, there's reason for concern once again.

The Knights are sitting on a hot bed of recruiting talent in Florida. The clock is ticking on becoming competitive. The brass over a proud program has to be getting antsy. Even though Frost isn't on the hot seat yet, there needs to be some upward trajectory within the program.

There is reason to worry that once the Big 12 season starts, it's going to be more of the same from UCF.

With Dan Mullen at the helm a season ago, UNLV was one of the biggest Group of Five surprises in the nation, finishing 10-3.

If it weren't for two close losses to Boise State (including in the league championship game), the Runnin' Rebels would have won the Mountain West Conference.

After some team shuffling in the new Pac-12, the Rebels were the preseason favorite to win the Mountain West this season. There was plenty of excitement surrounding former 5-star quarterback and Auburn transfer Jackson Arnold coming to Las Vegas for his third-and-final shot at stardom.

After splitting the first two games between Memphis (27-21 loss) and Hawaii (21-6 win), they were drilled by North Texas, 44-6, last week in a game that really set a negative tone for the rest of the season.

Now, who knows what's going to happen in league play? Mullen's team has been a colossal disappointment so far.

Sorry, Vanderbilt fans, Pavia Power isn't walking through that door.

Like a few other teams on this list, the Vanderbilt Commodores are 2-0 so far this season, but like Washington and others, it sure has been ugly.

For whatever reason, coach Clark Lea is deploying a two-quarterback system so far, with another (like former star Diego Pavia) New Mexico State transfer – Blaze Berlowitz – splitting snaps with true freshman Jared Curtis.

That wouldn't be such an awful thing if Curtis wasn't a former 5-star quarterback who stayed home by flipping from Georgia to sign with the Commodores and become the program's best (and maybe most important) recruit ever.

You don't sign kids with his talent for them to watch from the sidelines, especially when the season hasn't started well. After a slogging 28-9 win over FCS opponent Austin Peay to start the season, Vandy out-dueled Delaware 35-26 last week.

Curtis accounted for three touchdowns against the Blue Hens, so maybe Lea will leave him in, take his lumps and let him develop. That would be the best move because things could get rough when league play begins.

This weekend's nonconference tilt with North Carolina State may be a season-swing game.

Two years ago, Washington nearly made it all the way back to the top of the college football world when it lost to Michigan in the national championship game.

Kalen DeBoer left for Alabama shortly thereafter. The Huskies nabbed Jedd Fisch from Arizona to usher in their move to the Big Ten. They haven't reached that level of success since then, but they've been on the cusp of being good.

At worst, U-Dub is a tough out in a strong conference. With Demond Williams Jr. returning for his junior year, Washington was expected to be very dangerous, led by one of the most dynamic players in the sport.

Like Michigan, Washington is 2-0. But after sleepwalking through a season-opening Apple Cup win over rival Washington State, the Huskies were worse in Week 2. Utah State threw an incomplete Hail Mary in the end zone that would have beaten the Huskies, who won 16-14.

Fisch has lots of teaching moments from the first two games. The Huskies still have all the goals in front of them, but they look far from playoff-worthy (or even like an eight-win team) right now.

articles.title: Tolón pide "no perder los valores del deporte" tras los mensajes de Ceuta en futbolistas
articles.standfirst: La ministra de Educación y Deportes cree que la actuación de Mbappé, Konaté y Vinicius es "una decisión personal"
articles.summary: La ministra de Educación y Deportes cree que la actuación de Mbappé, Konaté y Vinicius es "una decisión personal"
articles.body: La ministra de Educación y Deportes, Milagros Tolón, ha advertido este miércoles que "los valores del deporte nunca se tienen que perder" tras la polémica suscitada después de que algunos clubes de fútbol de LaLiga hayan hecho salir a los jugadores al campo con mensajes de apoyo a Ceuta. Tolón ha dicho a los periodistas al llegar al Congreso que no vio las imágenes de anoche del partido en Elche en el que los futbolistas del Real Madrid Mbappé, Konaté y Vinícius enrollaron las camisetas para cortar el mensaje sobre Ceuta y se las quitaron antes que los demás. No obstante, ha añadido que es "una decisión personal" de esos futbolistas y que su opinión es que "el deporte es el deporte y los valores del deporte nunca se tienen que perder". Preguntada también en los pasillos del Congreso otra ministra socialista, la de Vivienda, Isabel Rodríguez, ha dicho que con los mensajes en las camisetas de futbolistas "hay que intentar evitar polemizar". Otra ministra, Mónica García, titular de Sanidad y líder de Más Madrid, ha apuntado que tampoco vio las imágenes de Elche, pero que le parece que "el tema de Ceuta ha sido utilizado nuevamente de manera torticera por la derecha". A los ceutíes les han llegado miles de migrantes y también "miles de discursos xenófobos", ha agregado García, así como que "los que tenemos empatía" podemos entender a los ceutíes por la "ruptura de la normalidad" por los miles de migrantes, pero también entender a estos, "que huyen del hambre y la desesperación". "Se pueden hacer gestos de apoyo a Ceuta, lo que es hipócrita es hacer gestos de apoyo a Ceuta para intentar impedir que la normalidad de Ceuta llegue, como hace el Partido Popular", ha explicado. Por su parte, Andrés Ibáñez, diputado de Compromís y Sumar, ha defendido la "libertad de expresión" de los futbolistas y ha pedido a la Asociación Valenciana de Empresarios, "particularmente al señor Boluda y el señor Roig", dado que es la promotora de que algunos equipos de fútbol saltaran al campo esta jornada liguera con esos mensajes, que al ser "muy amigos del PP y Vox" pidan a la Generalitat Valenciana que acoja a menores migrantes "que tienen que salir ya de Ceuta". "Ayudar a Ceuta no puede servir para dividir en base a sensibilidades de identidad nacional o incluso para espolear al racismo", ha subrayado Ibáñez.

articles.summary: La pelota está en el tejado de Loren Juarros, director deportivo que puede fichar tras la lesión de Lobete
articles.body: El mercado del Málaga sigue abierto por la lesión de Lobete. El administrador judicial incidió en esta cuestión; Muñoz dejó un mensaje claro ante la prensa. El Málaga dispone de capacidad económica para realizar una incorporación, aunque remitió la decisión deportiva a Loren Juarros. "Preguntadle a Loren, que es el director deportivo y el encargado de esa parcela. Mi preocupación es que todo funcione, pero dinero hay para fichar, ahora o cuando sea", explicó. De esta forma, el club mantiene abierta la puerta tanto a una incorporación de un futbolista que se encuentre actualmente sin equipo como a esperar hasta el próximo mercado de invierno. La decisión, en cualquier caso, deberá contar con el visto bueno de la dirección deportiva y del cuerpo técnico. Funes ya dejó claro el pasado viernes que el Málaga no quiere precipitarse pese a las necesidades existentes en la plantilla. «Hay predisposición a que se pueda generar ese espacio, pero precipitarnos ahora… Tenemos que asegurarnos de que el que llegue tiene que ayudar a los demás. Hay que tomar buenas decisiones ahora. Han salido nombres, pero hay que ver las circunstancias de incorporar ahora. El mercado está cerrado y tiene unas características distintas a lo de ahora», señaló el entrenador blanquiazul. El escenario se ha complicado especialmente en las últimas semanas. La lesión de ligamento cruzado de Lobete le dejará fuera durante toda la temporada, mientras que Aarón Ochoa ha sido intervenido del menisco externo y estará varios meses de baja. A ello se suma la situación de Haitam, lo que reduce considerablemente las alternativas disponibles en las posiciones de banda. En este contexto, nombres como Anthony Martial o Wilfried Zaha han aparecido entre las opciones que se han puesto sobre la mesa. Además, el rendimiento ofensivo de los extremos tampoco ha aportado goles en este inicio de campeonato. David Larrubia, Joaquín Muñoz y Juan Cruz todavía no han participado directamente en ningún tanto después de cinco jornadas. El Málaga únicamente ha marcado dos goles en Liga: el penalti transformado por Chupete y el tanto de Adrián Niño en Balaídos, a pase de Pablo Martínez tras un saque de esquina.

articles.title: Vini Jnr, Mbappe and Konate obscure Ceuta message ahead of Real Madrid match
articles.summary: Vini Jnr, Mbappe and Konate cover up Ceuta message of support ahead of Real Madrid's match against Elche.
articles.body:
Kylian Mbappe, Vinicius Junior and Ibrahima Konate rolled up their pre-game T-shirts ahead of Real Madrid's match at Elche on Tuesday to obscure the message of support for the people of Ceuta.

Ceuta is a Spanish autonomous city on the North African coast, bordering Morocco and separated from mainland Spain by the Strait of Gibraltar.

Players from both sides walked on to the pitch at Elche's ground, Martinez Valero, wearing white T-shirts carrying the message "Todos somos caballas" – translated as "We are all Ceutans" – along with references to the Spanish autonomous city.

While most of the players wore the shirts fully, Mbappe, Vinicius and Konate had theirs rolled up to around chest height, obscuring some of the slogan.

Mbappe and Vinicius then removed their shirts before the pre-match handshake, while Konate kept his on for longer. Their team-mates and the Elche players continued to wear the shirts through the pre-match formalities.

This is not the first time Real Madrid have shown support for Ceuta. Before their Champions League meeting with Inter Milan at the Santiago Bernabeu on 8 September, supporters in the south stand displayed cards featuring the coat of arms of the autonomous city, while the rest of the stadium joined the tribute with a round of applause.

The initiative was part of a wider show of support for Ceuta, following a major migration crisis in the Spanish territory after thousands of people entered from Morocco.

At least 72,000 migrants crossed from Morocco into Ceuta on 30 and 31 July. Most swam around a border fence and at least 100 people died during the crossing, according to figures from Ceuta's mayor.

Although most returned, as many as 5,000 remain in makeshift camps or are sleeping on the city's streets and beaches, leading to unrest in the autonomous Spanish city in North Africa.

Locals have expressed safety concerns and some have destroyed shelters and blocked aid being supplied to the migrants.

The representatives of the players have been asked for comment.

The episode came shortly before a dramatic night for Real Madrid, who recovered from surrendering a two-goal lead to beat Elche 3-2, with Carlos Espi scoring the winner in stoppage time.

Mbappe was among Madrid's scorers, while Vinicius started the game.

The pre-match gesture also highlighted the differing approaches among players and clubs to the Ceuta campaign.

Barcelona did not take part in the initiative, while players at other La Liga fixtures had worn the shirts as intended.

articles.title: Mensaje de Bordalás sobre su plantilla: "Somos el único equipo del fútbol profesional que no tiene extremos”
articles.standfirst: El técnico pide a su equipo atención para evitar que se escapen puntos: "No nos ha servido ponernos por delante para ganar partidos"
articles.summary: El técnico pide a su equipo atención para evitar que se escapen puntos: "No nos ha servido ponernos por delante para ganar partidos"
articles.body: El entrenador del Getafe, José Bordalás, compareció en sala de prensa este miércoles con motivo del duelo de mañana frente al Real Betis. El alicantino destacó que su equipo “es el único del fútbol profesional que no tiene extremos” y remarcó que el equipo piensa en hacer “un buen partido” frente a los de Pellegrini. Bajas: “ Tenemos dudas con algún jugador que acabó muy tocado. Quedan horas y confiamos en tener a la mayoría de jugadores”. Once: “No me gusta dar pistas, todavía quedan horas hasta el partido. Tenemos una idea de lo que puede dar el equipo y mañana, antes del partido, veremos quién juega”. Ponerse por delante: “Nunca sabes. El gol siempre es importante, sea en el minuto que sea, sirve para ponerse por delante. En estos últimos partidos no nos ha servido porque no nos ha permitido conseguir la victoria. Tenemos que aprender de ello, los detalles cuentan mucho. Contra el Betis no nos vale jugar bien por momentos, necesitamos hacer un partido completo durante los 90 minutos”. Qué falta: “Nos está faltando acierto. En el primer partido tuvimos en la primera media hora muchas opciones de ponernos por delante. El equipo está jugando bien por momentos, pero no nos vale con tener buenos momentos, necesitamos jugar bien y estar concentrados durante los 90 minutos. Los detalles penalizan. A nosotros nos penalizó contra el Celta el balón parado; contra el Dépor, un error y una pérdida en el medio campo, además de no fijar la marca de Aubameyang, y se nos fueron dos puntos”. Plantilla: “Nosotros tenemos que ir ajustando piezas. Todos sabéis que somos el único equipo del fútbol profesional que no tiene extremos y tienen que jugar jugadores en esa posición. En algún partido le ha tocado a Satriano. Esta temporada han salido muchos jugadores, han llegado nuevos y necesitan un periodo. El equipo está en construcción, pero LaLiga no perdona”. Real Betis: “Los resultados le avalan, lo vemos. No solamente en LaLiga, está sacando buenos resultados. Es un club que ha crecido mucho, se refuerza año tras año, va mejorando su plantilla y tiene alternativas. Está haciendo un buen inicio de Champions. Le avalan los resultados. Va a ser un partido tremendamente difícil, ya que es un equipo con un potencial enorme. Tiene una de las mejores plantillas de Europa”. Rotaciones: “No planteamos un partido pensando en el siguiente. Lo preparamos para intentar hacer un buen partido contra el Betis, con la intención de hacer un buen juego”. Joselu por delante de Mayoral: “Esa pregunta la podemos interpretar de manera positiva o negativa. Cuando no juegan chicos del filial se dice que no se cuenta con la cantera, pero cuando sí juegan se buscan otras opciones. El chico, con el esfuerzo y su trabajo, se está ganando tener minutos en Primera División”. Menos descanso del Betis: “No pensamos en ello, puesto que a veces nos ha ocurrido a nosotros, el tener no un día sino dos días menos. El Betis tiene alternativas, puede hacer dos equipos y no sabríamos cuál es el titular y cuál el suplente. No pienso en esa posibilidad. Pensamos en nosotros, en el esfuerzo del último partido, en recuperar y hacer un equipo lo más competitivo posible”. Conference: “No podemos pensar en otra competición que no sea LaLiga. Nuestra mente está puesta en ella. A nosotros lo que nos da de comer es LaLiga, tenemos que centrar el esfuerzo en ella. Bastantes dificultades tenemos como para pensar en la Conference. Ya llegará”. Kiko Femenía: “Está en ese proceso de readaptación. Tuvo una lesión en el isquio. Vamos a ver si para el partido de Málaga podría llegar, pero entendemos que puede ser justo, así que probablemente hasta después del parón no podremos contar con él”.

articles.title: Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca says it is 'quite poor' to focus on VAR controversy despite win at Manchester United
articles.summary: Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca says it is "quite poor" that the controversy surrounding Erling Haaland's winner has overshadowed his side's win at Manchester United.
articles.body:
Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca says it is "quite poor" that the controversy surrounding Erling Haaland's winner has overshadowed his side's performance at Manchester United on Sunday.

Haaland's goal on the hour mark, which was awarded after the virtual assistant referee ruled in City's favour, secured a 1-0 Premier League victory despite the visitors playing the majority of the derby at Old Trafford with 10 men following Phil Foden's red card.

The VAR decision was subsequently ruled to be incorrect by the referees' body and the aftermath of City's fourth successive league win has been dominated by the fall out from the incident.

"Talking about one episode or one moment after that game when we played for 70- 75 minutes with 10 players, I think it's quite poor," Maresca said, speaking before Thursday's Carabao Cup third-round tie against Norwich City.

"I think the performance was unbelievable, and I'm pleased with the performance."

Haaland's goal was initially disallowed on the field for offside but the VAR review found the striker was just onside, and the goal was awarded.

However, it soon became apparent that the officials had made an error in failing to identify an offside offence by Enzo Fernandez, diving at the ball in a central position and interfering with opponents.

"There is knowledge that there was a mistake and that's all. Sometimes it goes for you, sometimes against you. It's football," the Italian said.

Maresca, who succeeded Pep Guardiola in the summer, said previous VAR decisions have gone against City, including in a 2-1 defeat by United in January 2023.

"Three years ago when I was here [as Guardiola's assistant], it happened the exact same against United," he said.

"The goal was not a regular goal and no one apologised. We are still waiting for the apology for that."

Premier League refereeing body Pro Ref's chief Howard Webb has admitted the VAR did not consider whether Fernandez was offside before Haaland turned home the winner.

"I was really disappointed with this outcome. We all are," said Webb, speaking on 'Match Officials Mic'd Up'.

"None more so than the officials themselves. They take a lot of personal pride in what they do and they're obviously hurting now, having fallen short in this situation."

Foden was sent off for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes in the 23rd minute and United hit the post either side of half-time before the Norwegian's controversial goal on Sunday.

"The VAR gets super-focused on Haaland," said Webb. "He establishes he's onside, he thinks that's a good goal.

"He doesn't truly evaluate the full impact of Fernandez's position. He has a look to see if he touches the ball, because then that relates to potentially knocking it to Haaland, who goes on to score."

City host Norwich on Thursday (19:30 BST) before returning to league action against Sunderland on Sunday, 20 September (14:00).

articles.title: Rafa Marín, una alegría para Allegri: "Me siento más fuerte que nunca"
articles.standfirst: El central español ha sido titular en todos los partidos que ha disputado el Nápoles
articles.summary: El central español ha sido titular en todos los partidos que ha disputado el Nápoles
articles.body: "Está a punto de comenzar una temporada única, la temporada del Centenario, y todos lo sentimos. Quiero ayudar a este gran club y hacer historia junto al equipo. Por eso vine a quedarme, a luchar hasta el final por esta camiseta y por toda la gente que ama al 'Napoli", aseguró Rafa Marín (Guadajoz, 2002) tras completar 31 partidos -marcó un gol y dio una asistencia- durante su cesión al Villarreal la temporada pasada. Su gran temporada con el Alavés provocó que el Nápoles pagara 12 millones al Real Madrid en 2024 para hacerse con sus servicios. Su estreno en el 'calcio', a las órdenes de Antonio Conte, no fue fácil. Estuvo, de hecho, cerca de salir rumbo a Villarreal y Como en el mercado invernal, pero se quedó y puso su pequeño 'granito de arena' -disputó seis partidos- a la reconquista del 'Scudetto'. La experiencia de curtirse e ir al límite, tanto con Conte como Marcelino, le ha permitido regresar "reforzado" a nivel personal a un Nápoles en pleno cambio de ciclo. Poco a poco, sin hacer ruido, se ha hecho fuerte a las órdenes de Massimiliano Allegri, al que ya se enfrentó la pasada temporada en Champions, cuando dirigía a la Juventus (2-2). "No son palabras bonitas. Son hechos, trabajo y compromiso. Éste ha sido mi objetivo desde el primer día de la pretemporada. Me siento más fuerte que nunca, me siento preparado y tengo un enorme deseo de demostrarlo en el campo", advertía Rafa Marín. Ha tenido, también, la dosis de suerte necesaria. Las lesiones de Buongiorno y Marianucci, la posible salida de Beukema, el fichaje fallido de Mario Gila y las complicaciones para cerrar la llegada de Benoît Badiashile... le ayudó a hacerse fuerte junto a Rrahmani en el eje de la zaga. "Ahora es diferente. Cuando Rafa llegó, el equipo no disputaba la Champions y yo jugué los 38 partidos. Va a ser una temporada larga y vamos a necesitar a todos. Se ha convertido en un jugador fuerte", admite el propio Rrahmani. "Rafa Marín y Rrahmani están rindiendo bien. Es correcto mantenerlos", sostiene Diego Maradona Jr. Titular en los cinco partidos que ha disputado el Nápoles hasta la fecha, la victoria ante el Bolonia (1-0) le sirvió para redimirse de sus buenas actuaciones, sin premio, en las derrotas contra Inter (3-2) y Arsenal (0-1). "Jugó un buen partido -fue sustituido por calambres-. Me alegro por él. Es un buen jugador y necesitaba un partido así", reconocía Allegri para referirse a Rafa Marín, que pasa por ser el jugador del Nápoles con más interceptaciones (2) en Serie A, el segundo que más despejes completa (16) y que más pases buenos da (202 de 214), el cuarto que más 'tackles' (entradas) realiza con éxito (5 de 8), el quinto que más duelos gana (13 de 36) y el quinto con más recuperaciones (11). "El trabajo duro siempre da sus frutos. Necesitábamos esta primera victoria con nuestra gente. Sigamos trabajando, creciendo y siguiendo nuestro camino, todos juntos. ¡Forza 'Napoli' Sempre!", destacaba Rafa Marín vía 'Instagram'. Allegri tiene motivos para estar contento.

articles.title: Javier Tebas: "Salir con la camiseta doblada es como salir sin ella"
articles.standfirst: El presidente de la patronal del fútbol ve "muy mal" que tres jugadores del Real Madrid no lucieran camiseta de apoyo a Ceuta
articles.summary: El presidente de la patronal del fútbol ve "muy mal" que tres jugadores del Real Madrid no lucieran camiseta de apoyo a Ceuta
articles.body: El presidente de LaLiga, Javier Tebas, ha confesado que ve "muy mal" que tres jugadores del Real Madrid no lucieran una camiseta de apoyo a Ceuta este martes en el partido que los enfrentaba al Elche. "Me parece muy mal", ha afirmado Tebas durante una conferencia organizada en Huesca por la Asociación de Directivos y Ejecutivos de Aragón (ADEA), con relación a que Vinicius Jr., Mbappé y Konaté salieran al estadio Martínez Valero de Elche con la camiseta doblada, de modo que no se leía el mensaje de apoyo hacia el pueblo ceutí. Tebas ha indicado que el Real Madrid es una entidad española y la participación de toda la plantilla en este tipo de iniciativas responde a "un acto institucional, un acto de club" y no a "un acto personal donde haya que dar una opinión". Según ha explicado, los actos promovidos por entidades deportivas son autorizados por LaLiga y no deben quedar sujetos a la opinión de los futbolistas "cuando no afectan a cuestiones ideológicas". "Salir toda la plantilla con la camiseta es un acto de club. El jugador tiene que salir con la camiseta. Porque salir con la camiseta doblada es como salir sin ella", ha insistido Tebas, quien ha rechazado que se trate de una reivindicación política. En ese sentido, también ha se pronunciado sobre la polémica que rodea al jugador marroquí Ez Abde, quien sí portó la camiseta de apoyo a Ceuta en el partido Villarreal-Betis y ha recibido amenazas e insultos por ello, y lo ha calificado como "daño colateral".

articles.title: FIFA to present review of Infantino’s shelved investment plan to Council
articles.summary: A review of FIFA President Gianni Infantino’s failed World Cup selloff to be presented to governing body’s Council.
articles.body:
FIFA said ‌on Thursday that a review of the withdrawn FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal ⁠would be presented ⁠to the world football body’s Council, after Denmark’s football chief Jesper Moller criticised the lack of answers regarding ⁠the abandoned project.

Last week, Moller criticised world football’s governing body for declining to answer what he described as “critical questions” at a Legal Committee ⁠meeting about the scrapped proposal, launched by FIFA President Gianni Infantino, to sell commercial stakes in tournaments to outside investors.

“FIFA Standing Committees advise and assist the FIFA Council in their respective fields in line with FIFA’s ‌Statutes and Governance Regulations,” FIFA told the Reuters news agency in a statement.

“As previously communicated, a review of the withdrawn FIFA Forward Enterprise proposal will be presented to the FIFA Council.”

The FIFA Council comprises 37 members, including President Infantino, eight vice-presidents and 28 members elected by FIFA’s member associations.

Infantino’s proposal to sell a 20 percent stake in the World Cup ⁠and other FIFA events triggered a global backlash, ⁠with UEFA, the AFC and CONCACAF among the confederations calling for changes to FIFA’s leadership structure. The possibility of a no-confidence vote against Infantino was also discussed.

Several European national ⁠associations have since withdrawn support for Infantino’s re-election bid, with Greek Football Association President Makis Gagatsis and ⁠former Germany national team Director Oliver Bierhoff ⁠joining UEFA’s push for change in FIFA’s leadership on Tuesday, underscoring a united European front.

However, multiple sources familiar with the discussions told Reuters that the FIFA president retains sufficient backing ‌to secure another term, meaning opponents will need to shift strategy and focus on curbing his powers.

The FIFA presidential election is scheduled for ‌March ‌18, 2027, in Rabat, where Infantino will seek a fourth term in office.
